title: Numerics robustness options for poor meshes: warped-face gradient correction, secondary gradient limiting, boundary-gradient treatments, pressure-interpolation variants, solution limits
acceptance: Manufactured-solution order-of-accuracy test on skewed, warped and stretched meshes recovers the design order and the options do not degrade it on good meshes
note: DONE: acceptance met by non-ignored tests (m1_m4, m5). Outside the acceptance and still open: pressure-interpolation variants, a separate warped-face correction, case-tree wiring of GradientOptions. ADR 0016 wave 13. Library: GradientOptions (face-gradient correction, secondary limiter, boundary-gradient treatment) in rcfd-fv; case-level solution limits limits.temperature/scalar with clipped-cell count. MET: MMS order on skewed, warped and stretched meshes (>= 1.7 with the options off and with correction, >= 1.5 with the limiter; measured 1.76 to 2.04 except stretched 1.74 at n=32, all in limit). Options cost <= 4.6 percent error on near-orthogonal meshes. Limits clip to the band to 1e-14. On the affine skewed mesh the correction raises the error constant (2.1x) while keeping the order: no benefit is claimed. Registered mild mesh missed its non-orthogonality precondition (13.96 deg) and was replaced by a 0.015 amplitude mesh (disclosed). NOT delivered: pressure-interpolation variants, a warped-face correction separate from the face correction, case-tree wiring of the gradient options. WAVE 40B (ADR 0098): M5 adds n = 64 on the stretched mesh; all runs converge under the unchanged rule (change <= 1e-13 of the range, 600 sweeps) and the 32 -> 64 L2 order is 1.908 for C0, C1 and C2 (limit 1.7; the options are inert on this orthogonal mesh), so the asymptotic range is reached. DONE: acceptance met by non-ignored tests (m1_m4, m5). Outside the acceptance and still open: pressure-interpolation variants, a separate warped-face correction, case-tree wiring of GradientOptions. F-256 (ADR 0190, branch f256-gradient-wiring, not merged): the gradient options are wired into the case tree as solver.gradient_*. F-246 (ADR 0193, branch f246-pressure-interp, not merged): pressure-interpolation variants of the steady kernel, solver.pressure_interpolation; partial.

title: Adaptive time stepping and convergence accelerators: error-estimator steps, period-based steps, RMS/MAX Courant criteria, local timescale factors, residual smoothing, extrapolated step initialisation, nonlinear (Aitken-type) acceleration, stretched-mesh pseudo-time acceleration
acceptance: Error-controlled stepping (step doubling, `solver.error_tolerance`) on a two-timescale linear decay (rates differing by at least 100, both modes of unit initial amplitude) reaches its requested error without a user-chosen step: the final error E satisfies E / (tol T) within [0.3, 3] for two tolerances a factor 4 apart; on the Taylor-Green vortex the error-controlled global error scales with the tolerance (E / (tol T) within [0.3, 3]); a high-aspect-ratio flat-plate boundary-layer mesh converges to Blasius and turbulent skin-friction values within the unaccelerated tolerance
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv,linalg. Still PARTIAL: the flat-plate clause is open (residual smoothing, local timescale factors, stretched-mesh acceleration, Aitken in the outer loop also not delivered). WAVE 42A (ADR 0105) meets the first clause as worded on 2026-10-22; e2 shows the library controller, not the case path free of a chosen step. The Taylor-Green clause is met by S4 (E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90). The acceptance was reworded twice by USER DECISION (2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22), each after a check MISSED; those misses are kept as the ignored tests t1_..._known_miss and e1_..._known_miss. Depends on the pseudo-transient option being finished. WAVE 17A (ADR 0023): Only a library building block, ddt::ErrorController, exists (not wired to the tree). Linear-decay acceptance missed (81 vs 76 steps relative scale, 46 vs 36 absolute reference), recorded as ignored known-miss tests. Taylor-Green, flat-plate acceleration, residual smoothing and Aitken acceleration not delivered; status then todo. WAVE 27B (ADR 0050): rcfd_fv::stepctl and the case keys solver.max_courant_rms, dt_safety/growth/shrink, min_dt/max_dt, error_tolerance (step doubling, implicit Euler), period/steps_per_period, extrapolate_initial, output.write_times/write_time_interval (exact landing, restart-safe). Taylor-Green: Courant control needs 74 steps vs 113 fixed (limit 0.75x) at 1.7 percent L2 difference. Error control E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90 with halving ratio 1.93-2.00. Variable-step BDF2 order 1.95. Extrapolated start halves the initial residual (median ratio 0.14). NAMED GAPS: Aitken relaxation is a library building block only (not in the PIMPLE outer loop or the tree). Local timescale factors, residual smoothing, the stretched-mesh pseudo-time acceleration and the flat-plate acceptance are not delivered. Step control excludes energy/scalar/turbulence/dynamic-mesh runs. Error control is implicit Euler only. Compressible solver not covered. WAVE 39C (ADR 0094), still PARTIAL: the fixed-step side of the Taylor-Green comparison is now measured. Uniform implicit-Euler step counts N = 1, 2, ... were run against the same BDF2 reference: the smallest N with L2 error <= 0.02 is 64 (error 1.97e-2), and the smallest with error <= the Courant-controlled run's 1.69e-2 is 72; the Courant-controlled run takes 74 steps. The registered limit (74 < 64) is MISSED, kept as the ignored test t1_..._known_miss in rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs. For a single decaying mode a Courant controller (itself fixed-CFL stepping) cannot beat the best uniform step; ADR 0094 proposes (not applied) rewording the first clause to a two-timescale linear decay under error control plus the already measured Taylor-Green tolerance scaling (S4). Linear-decay misses, the flat-plate clause, residual smoothing, local timescale factors and stretched-mesh acceleration remain open. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: acceptance reworded to the two-timescale form proposed in ADR 0094 (Courant control cannot beat the best uniform step on a single mode). Still partial: the two-timescale test does not exist yet; S4 covers the Taylor-Green scaling; flat-plate clause open. WAVE 41A (ADR 0101, rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs e1): the reworded two-timescale clause was tested and MISSED, as predicted in the ADR before the run. Shear wave u_x = sin y + sin 12y on a periodic 4 x 64 box (rates 0.999 and 128.1, ratio 128; one PISO step equals the implicit-Euler factors to 1.7e-15), T = 1, S4 controller settings: tol 1e-2 takes 1913 controlled steps (E 7.84e-3) against 64 uniform steps at equal error; tol 2.5e-3 takes 3149 against 240. Kept as the ignored e1_..._known_miss with the limit unchanged. Reason (derived in ADR 0101): an error-per-unit-time controller spends about lambda_fast/(4 tol) steps resolving the fast transient, which L-stable uniform implicit Euler damps without resolving; it can only win once the slow mode has decayed by about e^-(rate ratio). So the clause as reworded is not expected to be met by local error control on a decaying linear system; this is for the user to decide. The Taylor-Green clause is met by S4 (E/(tol T) 0.87-0.90). The flat-plate clause is still open. Stays partial. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: acceptance reworded a second time. Wave 41A (ADR 0101) showed error control cannot beat the best uniform step count on a linear decay (1913 steps vs 64 at tol 1e-2): per-unit-time control resolves the fast transient that implicit Euler merely damps. New first clause: error control hits the requested error with no hand-picked step. The step-count test e1 stays as an ignored known miss. Flat-plate clause still open. WAVE 42A (ADR 0105, rcfd-fv tests/adaptive_step.rs e2, non-ignored): the first clause as worded on 2026-10-22 is MET. Same shear wave as E1 (rates 0.999 and 128.1, unit amplitudes), T = 1, error = relative L2 time error against the exact semi-discrete solution. No step chosen by the user: library controller defaults (no min_dt / max_dt), only error_tol set, first proposal = T. tol 1e-2: 2502 steps (18 rejected), E 7.917e-3, E/(tol T) 0.792; tol 2.5e-3: 9989 steps (20 rejected), E 2.080e-3, 0.832 (limit [0.3, 3]). Limitation recorded: through the case keys the run still needs solver.dt (timectl takes the first proposal and max_dt from it and min_dt = 1e-3 solver.dt by default), so e2 shows the library controller, not the case path free of a chosen step; not changed (default change). e1 stays ignored. Still PARTIAL: the flat-plate clause is open (residual smoothing, local timescale factors, stretched-mesh acceleration, Aitken in the outer loop also not delivered).

title: Non-iterative time advancement (fractional-step) option for transient flow
acceptance: Taylor-Green vortex decay matches the analytic solution within 2 percent; transient lid-driven cavity agrees with published data
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Three registered checks MISSED and are ignored known-miss tests: BDF2 temporal order, spatial ratio (met after the wave 25A fix) and the Kim-Moin boundary treatment. Alternative to the iterated PISO/PIMPLE loop for large steps and low cost. PARTIAL (wave 21C, ADR 0037). Delivered: solver.time_advance = fractional_step for the transient piso algorithm (Euler and BDF2). solver.fractional_form incremental or chorin. solver.fractional_boundary kim_moin or plain. One momentum predictor and ONE pressure Poisson solve per step (library PimpleSettings.fractional, module rcfd-fv pimple/fractional.rs) with a case-tree option and located errors. Measured: Taylor-Green kinetic-energy error 2.3e-3 (limit 0.02). Euler temporal order 1.034. Divergence 1.8e-11 default and 2.8e-15 tight solver tolerance. Difference to PISO 3.0e-3 (limit 5e-3). Lid-driven cavity Re 100 Ghia centreline error 3.0e-3 and 9.0e-3 (limit 0.02) and difference to SIMPLEC 4.7e-4 (limit 0.01). Tree equals library bit for bit. The roadmap acceptance is met by these checks, but three registered checks MISSED and are ignored known-miss tests: BDF2 temporal order 1.04 on the periodic Taylor-Green (band 1.7 to 2.3; wave 25A, ADR 0043: the lagged periodic partner value was a defect and is now extrapolated, order 1.51, the rest is the O(dt h^2) collocated pressure-smoothing term; a wall-bounded mode gives 2.07). Spatial ratio 2.48 (limit 3.0; met after the wave 25A fix, 3.95). The Kim-Moin boundary treatment shows no benefit in the Chorin form (ratio 1.13 against 0.5; the incremental form is insensitive to it). NOT delivered: rotational pressure correction, Crank-Nicolson, Choi-type transient Rhie-Chow, body force and buoyancy, turbulence, energy, rheology, pimple outer loops, moving meshes, restart of fractional runs, verification of the Kim-Moin and Zang et al. references (see docs/reference-data.md). DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Advection and transient scheme additions: high-resolution (bounded blended), compressive, specified blend factor, bounded central differencing, bounded second-order time scheme
acceptance: Order-of-accuracy test on a smooth advected profile gives the nominal order; square-wave advection stays within physical bounds; blend factor 0 and 1 reproduce the upwind and central results
note: Wave 39B (ADR 0093): DONE. The O1c convergence known miss stays ignored and unchanged as the record. Literature references unverified (docs/reference-data.md). ADR 0016 wave 13. Added: blended(beta) (0 = upwind and 1 = central to 0), gamma(beta_m), compressive(k) (Roe-Sweby family, k project-extended below 1), bounded_central (bitwise minmod in NVD form) convection schemes. The bdf2_bounded time scheme. MET: B1 blend 0/1 equal upwind/central (0, 0). Order on a smooth profile (central, blended(1), gamma, bounded_central 2.0000; first-order members 0.98 to 1.003). Square wave within 1e-3 of the bounds for gamma, compressive and bounded_central (dt = 0.1 h; the registered 0.5 h gave a toothless control). Temporal orders. MISS: O1c convergence for compressive(1.5) and compressive(2) (limit cycle at 1e-8 per sweep from limiter switching; orders in band), kept in an ignored known-miss test. Set-up deviations disclosed in the ADR results. Literature references unverified (docs/reference-data.md). Wave 39B (ADR 0093): DONE. New non-ignored test o1d_compressive_order_on_limit_cycle measures the order of compressive(1.5) and compressive(2) on the stationary limit cycle (20000 sweeps, 200-sweep error windows ending at sweeps 10000 and 20000 overlap at every n; worst-case orders over the cycle 1.9812..1.9818 and 1.9909..1.9911 for compressive(1.5), 1.9815..1.9816 and 1.9910 for compressive(2); registered band 1.85 to 2.3). The O1c convergence known miss stays ignored and unchanged as the record.

title: Enthalpy-porosity solidification and melting: liquid fraction, mushy-zone damping, pull velocity

title: Magnetohydrodynamic Lorentz-force coupling for liquid conductors
acceptance: Hartmann channel flow matches the analytic Hartmann velocity profile within 2 percent
note: The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Registered misses are ignored known_miss tests with limits intact, including the registered dt 0.02 Hartmann set-up (unstable) and solved-potential current cancellation 1e-6. PARTIAL (wave 23A, ADR 0039). Delivered: sources.<n> type lorentz (steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC): uniform imposed B, conductivity, optional applied E, J = sigma(E - grad phi + u x B) at low magnetic Reynolds number. Potential none (short circuit, explicit force plus implicit sigma B^2/rho sink) or solve (potential equation on the 21A electric solver with its boundary keys). Output fields lorentz_force and current_density. Measured Hartmann channel (periodic box_2d, no-slip plates): Profile error 1.6e-3, 6.5e-3, 6.5e-3 of u_max at Ha 2, 10, 20 (limit 2e-2). Flow-rate reduction error 1.2e-3, 8.6e-4, 4.1e-4 (limit 1e-2). Insulated walls Ha 10 the same. Lorentz integral, work identity and momentum balance at round-off. Electrode current within 1.5e-3. WAVE 25C (ADR 0045): the same lorentz source now works in transient PISO and PIMPLE (outer-iteration momentum-source hook); located errors for coupled and compressible. Measured: on a stable step nu dt/dy^2 = 1.6 the Hartmann cases meet the steady limits (profile error 1.6e-3, 6.5e-3, 6.5e-3; flow error 1.2e-3, 8.6e-4, 4.1e-4; last-step change <= 4.9e-14) and PISO/PIMPLE equal steady SIMPLEC to 4.7e-15/5.7e-14. Registered misses (ignored known_miss tests, limits intact): The registered dt 0.02 Hartmann set-up is unstable because transient PISO/PIMPLE diverges at nu dt/dy^2 above about 3 to 6 even without any source (pre-existing; WAVE 26A, ADR 0046: the periodic-box part was the lagged periodic partner of the transient momentum matrix, now implicit and fixed; the wall-bounded remainder is the splitting error of the non-converged pressure correctors at large nu dt/dy^2, a property of the scheme, not a coding defect). Solved-potential current cancellation 1e-6 is missed (8.6e-1 at dt 0.02; 8.05e-3 at dt 2.5e-4 with 3 outer iterations, 2.4e-7 at 24 outer iterations as a diagnostic). The periodic-box uniform-acceleration and impulse-balance checks miss because of the pre-existing lagged periodic momentum coupling. Not delivered: coupled solver, Joule heating, case-given or varying B, induced field, non-uniform sigma, a 3-D duct with side-wall layers or a non-trivial solved potential, published experiments. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Interface physics: thermal contact resistance, thin and shell conduction with layers, conditional (open/closed) connections, mapped coupled interfaces
acceptance: Two-solid contact with prescribed resistance reproduces the analytic series-resistance temperature jump within 1 percent; a layered thin wall matches the composite-wall solution
note: Priority P2. Size M. Area: fv. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Miss: the registered stiff transient enthalpy-drift limit (G5, dt 0.01) is not met. Builds on the conservative non-conformal interface. Wave 21A (ADR 0035): layered resistances (steady, no layer capacity) and open/closed connection in the case tree; series-resistance and layered-wall checks to round-off. Miss: the registered stiff transient enthalpy-drift limit (G5, dt 0.01) is not met (round-off 1e-11), corrected dt 1e-3 passes. Wave 25A (ADR 0043) diagnosis: the drift is the double-precision representation of the stiff matrix (Fourier number 8e3), not an interface defect. Not delivered: layer thermal capacity, in-plane shell conduction, solution-dependent switching, mapped interfaces. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Per-region model sets: assign energy, turbulence, species and radiation models per region and couple regions through interfaces
acceptance: A published conjugate heat transfer benchmark with a conducting wall is reproduced within published scatter using different model sets in fluid and solid regions
note: PARTIAL (wave 21B, ADR 0036). Missing (why partial): The turbulence transport equations are still solved inside laminar regions. Per-region energy, radiation and species models. Coupling of regions through interfaces. The published conjugate heat transfer benchmark with different model sets (the conjugate code was being changed by another wave). Delivered: regions.<name> section (zone all/box/cell_zone/register) with turbulence = model | laminar: the momentum equation uses the molecular viscosity on every face touching a laminar region (steady and transient incompressible runs). Measured: Laminar region over the whole domain equals a laminar run exactly (0 difference, limit 1e-6) while a partial region changes the solution (1.9e-4). Mask semantics exact. Located diagnostics for unknown values, empty zones, no turbulence model, RSM/plugin, rheology and temperature-dependent viscosity. Previous scope text: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv,api. Architectural item: region-scoped settings in the state tree.

title: Heat-exchanger domain model: shell-and-tube and dual-cell macro models, with fan, vent, porous-jump and network boundary types as sub-criteria
acceptance: Counterflow exchanger reproduces the effectiveness-NTU analytic result within 2 percent; fan and vent boundaries reproduce their prescribed pressure-flow curves
note: The acceptance is met (WAVE 39D, ADR 0095). The exchanger checks still verify the algebraic macro model, not a resolved exchanger, and shell-and-tube stays UNVERIFIED. Plain SIMPLEC with a velocity inlet and a forward vent diverges from the first iteration; this robustness defect is not fixed. Not delivered: segmented/resolved exchanger, multi-branch network, two-phase, fan total pressure with dynamic head. PARTIAL (wave 23A, ADR 0039). Delivered: rcfd_fv::hx (eps-NTU counter, parallel, crossflow with one stream mixed, shell and tube, both-unmixed fit; pressure-loss closure). Components heat_exchanger mode ntu (arrangement, UA, constant or dual-cell secondary, loss_coefficient/loss_linear on the downstream plane) and type fan_boundary (curve-driven pressure patch). Measured: Counterflow/parallel against eps-NTU and an independent marched solution to 1e-14 (limit 2e-2). Dual-cell energy exchange to 1e-8. Loss closure exact to 1e-14. Fan boundary flow within 6.3e-4 of the analytic operating point and patch pressure on the curve (limit 2e-3). The macro cell is algebraic, so these checks verify wiring, not a resolved exchanger. Misses (ignored known_miss tests, limits unchanged): The both-unmixed crossflow curve fit deviates up to 3.3 percent from the exact solution and breaks the small-N slope and parallel <= cross ordering. Shell and tube is UNVERIFIED against a published table. Vent and porous jump reuse ADR 0012/0022 evidence (no new CFD vent test); the fan test needs a distributed bed because a lossless pressure-pressure duct diverges in SIMPLEC. Not delivered: segmented/resolved exchanger, multi-branch network, two-phase, fan total pressure with dynamic head. WAVE 25C (ADR 0045): fan, porous jump, loss closure, fan_boundary and the NTU exchanger now also run in transient PISO/PIMPLE (pimple, 3 outer iterations). Fixed-point source check 9.0e-6. Fan flow 1.5e-5 and jump drop 2.2e-6. Loss closure 6e-14. fan_boundary flow 1.9e-13 and patch pressure 5e-15. NTU duty equal to the steady SIMPLEC duty to 1.4e-14 relative. Coupled and compressible algorithms give located errors and are not delivered. WAVE 25B (ADR 0044): the both-unmixed crossflow fit is replaced by the exact Poisson-tail series (worst deviation 7.7e-6 from a Richardson-extrapolated marched 2-D reference, limit 1e-4); the three H2/H3 known-miss tests now pass under --ignored and stay ignored with limits intact. WAVE 39D (ADR 0095): X6 fan boundary at three operating points (bed permeability 3e-7, 1e-6, 1e-5 on the X4 set-up): Q = 1.929e-2, 3.052e-2, 3.621e-2 against the analytic operating points within 1.13e-3, 6.35e-4, 8.6e-5 (limit 5e-3), one point on each curve segment; the patch pressure lies on the curve to 1.8e-13 (by construction). X7 vent on its own set-up (periodic duct, velocity inlet, vent with K = 2.5 at xmax) at u = 0.5, 1, 2, -0.5, -1, -2: the outlet pressure equals 0.5 K u|u| within 3.9e-13 (limit 1e-6), which separates the quadratic law from a linear one by a factor of 2. X7 uses pseudo-time at Courant number 1 (pseudo_dt = 0.02/|u|, ADR 0095 amendment 1). The registered fixed pseudo_dt 0.02 gives NaN at u = 2 (ignored test x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt_known_miss). Plain SIMPLEC with a velocity inlet and a forward vent diverges from the first iteration (max |ux| 6.06, 1.8e2, 1.8e5 at K = 2.5; stable at K = 0); this robustness defect is not fixed. The acceptance is met. The exchanger checks still verify the algebraic macro model, not a resolved exchanger, and shell-and-tube stays UNVERIFIED.

title: Actuator-disk (virtual blade) momentum source for rotors and propellers: blade-element lookup, tip loss, trim
acceptance: Axial hover thrust and induced velocity match momentum theory; a public model-rotor hover data set gives thrust within 10 percent
note: PARTIAL (wave 21B, ADR 0036). Missing (why partial): Blade-element lookup, tip loss and trim. Time-varying and rotating disks. The model-rotor hover data comparison (acceptance 10 percent) and any validated CFD hover induced-velocity result (A5 not attempted). Hover momentum-theory formulas are derived, not checked against a rotorcraft text. Delivered: rcfd-fv actuator.rs and sources type actuator_disk (steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC; WAVE 25C, ADR 0045: a steady-in-time disk also in transient PISO/PIMPLE, duct kinematic dp 50.0000 and velocity perturbation 1e-12, coupled/compressible give located errors): Thrust along a direction over a zone (box, cell_zone, register, all), uniform or linear-in-radius loading, optional swirl torque about the disk axis, force and torque exact to machine precision (3.7 N to 4e-16 relative, 0.7 N m to 1e-15). Smoothed distribution (default) that removes the edge-cell imbalance of a sharp top-hat. Momentum-theory closed forms (induced velocity, wake velocity, power, figure of merit, Betz coefficients) verified to 1e-13. Located diagnostics. Duct pressure jump: Corrected set-up (A4b) kinematic dp 50.0000 (limit 0.5), velocity perturbation 2.9e-12. The registered symmetry-wall set-up misses on velocity because the existing solver does not keep plug flow with symmetry side walls (0.159 even without a disk) and the sharp top-hat (distribution = cell) misses with a 3 m/s jet; both are ignored known-miss tests. Previous scope text: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. Momentum source distributed over a disk zone.

title: Immersed (non-conforming) solid domain with modified forcing
acceptance: Flow past a cylinder with an immersed solid matches the published DFG 2D-1 drag, lift and Strouhal number within 5 percent
note: PARTIAL (ADR 0218, 2026-11-07). Acceptance read as the DFG 2D-1 drag and lift (Re 20) and the DFG 2D-2 Strouhal number (Re 100; 2D-1 has none, ADR 0218 Q1), against the FeatFlow reference values. Delivered: rcfd-fv immersed.rs, an immersed solid (cylinder, sphere, cuboid, inverted, rigid velocity) as an implicit forcing in SimpleSolver and PimpleSolver (field immersed, default None, defaults bit-identical): volume penalisation of the solid cells and, in the first fluid cells, the modified forcing that imposes the no-slip value at the true crossing of the surface (the linear Dirichlet extrapolation written as a face coefficient); force and moment from the reaction of the forcing; refusals of the fractional step and moving meshes; rcfd_mesh::gen::box_2d_coords. Measured (limits registered before the code): 2D-1 on a Cartesian mesh of D/80 around the cylinder C_D 5.57834 (-0.02 %), C_L 0.0106900 (+0.67 %) (limit 5 %; observed orders 2.35 and 1.96 over D/20, D/40, D/80); 2D-2 on D/40, BDF2 PISO, St 0.30073 (-0.38 %; max C_D, max C_L within 2.6 % of FeatFlow); the forcing sum equals the momentum balance of the domain to 1.8e-13; the plain (unmodified) forcing gives C_D -1.95 % and C_L +4.76 % on D/40 against -0.17 % and +2.73 %. Missing (why partial): the immersed forcing is first order (KNOWN MISS: circular Couette between an immersed rotating cylinder and an immersed ring, observed order 1.02 against the registered 1.5, error 1.6e-3 of omega R1 at N 96, 8.6 times below the plain forcing; diagnosed as the Rhie-Chow mass flux across the staircase faces, not checked); no case-schema key or Studio control (a schema golden would change, Q2); no moving or deforming bodies (Q4); not in the block-coupled solver, the fractional step or on moving meshes; momentum only (no energy or scalars); 3-D shapes checked by their level sets only; the outlet is zero gradient, not do-nothing. Previous scope text: Priority P4. Size L. Area: fv,mesh. Speculative; validate need before scheduling.

title: Tabulated and piecewise material properties: pressure-temperature tables with saturation lines, piecewise-linear and piecewise-polynomial forms, nine-coefficient heat-capacity polynomials, compressible-liquid density, curve-fit viscosity laws, orthotropic conductivity
acceptance: Public water and steam verification values reproduced to the standard's table tolerance; saturation-line round trip closes; a compressible-liquid density law reproduces its defining relation
note: The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. KNOWN MISS: plain bilinear eval of the steam table is at 2.6e-4 against the registered 1e-4 and stays ignored. The water/steam acceptance rests on the existing IF97 module, not on new table data. PARTIAL (wave 21B, ADR 0036). Delivered: rcfd-core tabular.rs with piecewise-linear and piecewise-polynomial tables (located validation, monotonic checks, constant/linear/error extrapolation), Vogel-Fulcher-Tammann viscosity, the Tait compressible-liquid density law, and a pressure-temperature table with saturation line, phase selection and bilinear interpolation. Case-schema laws piecewise_linear, piecewise_polynomial and vogel in properties.viscosity / conductivity / specific_heat (defaults and baseline hashes unchanged). Measured: Interpolation exact at nodes. P1 table-vs-polynomial dT 4.4e-12 K. Kinked-conductivity Kirchhoff case 7.4e-2 K (limit 0.5). Vogel Couette 4.4e-5 U. Saturation interpolation 5.2e-4 (limit 1e-3), psat(tsat) round trip and phase selection pass. KNOWN MISS: the registered 1e-4 mid-cell interpolation error of the steam table is 2.64e-4 (liquid half 3.3e-5 passes) because steam is non-ideal in the pressure direction; kept as an ignored test, limit not widened. Missing (why partial): Orthotropic conductivity. NASA nine-coefficient heat capacity as a case law (exists in the reactor crate). Pressure-dependent properties (Tait density, P-T tables) are library-only and not connected to the incompressible solvers. CSV table-file property laws. The water/steam acceptance rests on the existing IF97 module, not on new table data. Tait and Vogel formulas verified against public pages (docs/reference-data.md). Previous scope text: Priority P2. Size M. Area: core,api. Public formulations only; no reference-fluid database import. WAVE 25B (ADR 0044): opt-in PtTable::eval_density_ideal_scaled meets the registered 1e-4 on the T9 vapour table (1.24e-5); plain bilinear eval is unchanged and its known miss (2.6e-4) stays ignored. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Non-equilibrium condensing (wet) steam in transonic flow
acceptance: Condensing steam in a converging-diverging nozzle reproduces the published wall-pressure trace and onset location within 5 percent
note: Priority P4. Size L. Area: fv. Needs an accurate real-gas steam model first. TODO by the decision rule of ADR 0217 (two mutations survived the fast checks); the acceptance comparison is met at library level. Delivered (ADR 0217): rcfd-fv::wetsteam, an explicit density-based Euler solver for the single-fluid wet-steam mixture (monodisperse droplets, classical nucleation with the Kantrowitz correction, Young's growth with alpha = 11, IF97 saturation line and liquid density, IAPWS surface tension, perfect-gas vapour), HLLC for the general EOS, point-implicit wetness; new rcfd-core::iapws functions (extended saturation line, saturation_temperature). Library only, opt-in; defaults and hashes unchanged. Acceptance (Moses and Stein case 203, digitized from Starzmann et al. GT2016-57598): centreline p/p0 within 5 percent at all 41 points (worst -4.93 percent at the exit), onset location +1.90 percent; droplet radius within 3.9 percent of r32. Checks: model values, isochoric relaxation and equilibrium, conservation, frozen wet shock tube, bit-identical dry limit against compressible.rs, quasi-1-D reference (0.16 percent), dry isentropic nozzle, grid study. NOT done or missed: mutations MU3 (nucleated-mass term) and MU6 (sound speed in the wave-speed estimates) survived; the coarse 230 x 10 run is not steady at its cap (8.2e-6); L1's first run missed its cell-spread limit (amendment 1, L1b met). No case keys (Q1), no real-gas vapour EOS (Q2), inviscid only (Q3), Moore nozzle B geometry not readable (Q4), no moments/polydispersion (Q5). Open questions Q1 to Q11 in ADR 0217.

title: Pollutant post-processing: thermal NOx (extended Zeldovich), prompt, fuel and N2O paths, moment-based soot

note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: reactor. PARTIAL (wave 18B, ADR 0027). title: Stiff chemistry acceleration: in-situ tabulation, dynamic mechanism reduction, clustering of similar cells
acceptance: 0D ignition delay of a published fuel/mechanism pair reproduced within 5 percent with acceleration enabled, with a documented speed-up
note: PARTIAL (wave 28B, ADR 0053). The 5 percent point is met only against the same mechanism integrated directly; comparison against a published ignition-delay measurement is NOT DELIVERED. Delivered: ISAT (Pope 1997) as a library with ellipsoid growth, element-active subspace and frozen-noise rule (crates/rcfd-reactor isat.rs). DRG static skeleton and dynamic per-step reduction (drg.rs). Leader clustering of similar cells with increment transfer, tolerance 0 bit-identical (cluster.rs). Case keys chemistry.acceleration (off|cluster|isat) and chemistry.accel_tolerance on the transient finite_rate step, chemistry.json acceleration object. Measured: 0D H2/air ignition delay with ISAT 1.7e-3 and with dynamic DRG 1.6e-3 relative difference to the direct integration (limit 5e-2), speed-up 118 for cell ISAT on repeated states and 5.4 to 9 for DRG (reported only). MISSES (ignored known-miss tests, limits intact): ISAT retrieval error 1.27e-3 against 1e-3 on the heated ensemble. Element drift 2.4e-9 against 1e-9. The profile test (cells did not ignite, 0 against 17 above 1500 K). NOT DELIVERED: comparison against a published ignition-delay measurement (the 5 percent point is met only against the same mechanism integrated directly), acceleration of steady or EDC closures, parallel tables. Priority P3. Size L. Area: reactor. Parallel-memory dependency deliberately dropped; works in shared memory.

title: Interfacial mass transfer catalogue: evaporation-condensation (temperature or pressure driven), species-equilibrium transfer (Raoult, Henry), wall condensation
acceptance: 1D Stefan evaporation matches the analytic solution; film condensation agrees with the Nusselt solution within 10 percent
note: PARTIAL (wave 23B library, ADR 0040; wave 28A wiring into the VOF host and case tree, ADR 0052). The 1D Stefan evaporation acceptance and the CFD-level film condensation within 10 percent of Nusselt are missing. There is no energy equation in the multiphase path, so the temperature is a PRESCRIBED field. Lee, ZGB factor values, Schrage factor and Rohsenow 0.68 are from knowledge and UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md). WAVE 28A: Lee and Hertz-Knudsen-Schrage mass transfer is wired into the VOF host (rcfd-fv vof.rs) and the case tree (multiphase.mass_transfer). Source in the alpha equation (exponential integrator of the frozen-temperature relaxation for Lee, alpha stays in [0, 1]) and the continuity volume source mdot (1/rho_v - 1/rho_l) in the pressure equation (solve_pressure_src); the same delivered rate feeds both. Checks M1-M5 pass: closed form 1.4e-14, per-cell phase balance 2.2e-16, coupled volume identity 9.2e-16, continuity 2.1e-13, zero transfer at saturation bit-identical, Hertz-Knudsen 1.1e-15; tree equals library. LIMITATIONS: there is no energy equation in the multiphase path, so the temperature is a PRESCRIBED field (uniform plus constant gradient), the latent heat only enters p_sat and a reported power, there is no latent-heat feedback, no 1D Stefan problem or boiling run, and no phase-change term in the momentum rho phi; a pressure patch is required; the rate is clipped to the phase available in the cell. Library delivered in wave 23B: rcfd-fv masstransfer.rs, per-cell source evaluators taking phase fractions, temperatures and pressures: Lee temperature-driven and Hertz-Knudsen-Schrage kinetic evaporation-condensation. A pressure-driven bubble-dynamics form derived from Rayleigh-Plesset (Zwart-Gerber-Belamri structure). Raoult bubble/dew pressures and Henry's law with van 't Hoff temperature dependence. Species transfer rate. Nusselt laminar-film wall condensation (film thickness, wall mass flux, mean coefficient 0.943 form). A 0-D Lee relaxation cell. Checked against hand values and closed forms (to 1e-13 and better), exact phase-source conservation (liquid + vapour == 0, energy == -mdot h_fg), zero at saturation, sign logic, kinetic-theory maximum flux, Nusselt mass-flow identity, and the frozen-mass relaxation analytic solution (6e-11 relative); located errors for bad inputs. All M1-M9 checks pass, no misses. Missing (why partial): An Euler-Euler host. Energy-equation coupling and the 1D Stefan evaporation acceptance (needs an energy equation and a moving-interface solver). The CFD-level film condensation within 10 percent of Nusselt. Activity-coefficient equilibrium models. Interfacial-area transport (F-228). Lee, ZGB factor values, Schrage factor and Rohsenow 0.68 are from knowledge and UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md). Previous scope text: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. Source-term closures on top of the multiphase base.

title: Free-surface wave generation and absorption: linear and Stokes wave inlets, irregular spectrum waves, numerical beach damping
acceptance: Linear dispersion relation and Stokes wave elevation reproduced; reflected-wave fraction below 5 percent with the beach
note: PARTIAL (wave 23B library, ADR 0040; wave 28A wiring into the VOF host and case tree, ADR 0052). The full tank acceptance beyond the coarse 2-D checks of wave 28A is missing. WAVE 28A did not deliver a refinement study, Stokes-2 or irregular waves in a tank run, 3-D tanks or a comparison with published tank data. WAVE 28A: a wave-inlet boundary (per-face velocity and alpha from Airy / Stokes-2 kinematics with a ramp) and a relaxation-zone beach (still-water target, exponential or polynomial weights) are wired into the VOF host and the case tree (multiphase.waves, multiphase.reference_point). Coarse 2-D tank (depth 0.30 m, T 1 s, H 0.06 m, lambda/32): Wave height -10.5 percent at 0.5 lambda and -18.0 percent at 1.5 lambda (limits 12 and 25, numerical damping stated in the ADR before the runs), periods within 0.5 percent. Beach K_r 0.014 against the control wall 0.524 (20 periods; Goda-Suzuki two-gauge method; limits 0.15 and 0.5). Volume identity 6e-14, level drift 1.4e-3 m (limit 6e-3), alpha bounded. Inlet values reproduce the wave to 1e-16 m. KNOWN MISSES (ignored tests, limits intact): The 10-period control (set-up defect, window before the reflected group returns; corrected 20-period tests pass). Still water with the zone and 3 PISO correctors (max|U| 1.3e-8 against 1e-10: base PISO splitting error of the thin air layer, identical without the zone; with 4 correctors 8e-12 passes). Not delivered: a refinement study, Stokes-2 or irregular waves in a tank run, 3-D tanks, comparison with published tank data, relaxation to a wave target in the tree. Library delivered in wave 23B: rcfd-fv waves.rs: Finite-depth dispersion solved to 2e-15 residual. Airy and second-order Stokes kinematics (elevation, velocity, potential, pressure) usable as wave-inlet values with a start-up ramp and an exact liquid-volume-fraction helper. Irregular waves from Pierson-Moskowitz and JONSWAP spectra with a seeded reproducible phase set (recovered Hs within 4.8e-4 and 3.3e-4 of target, moments m1 and m2 within 2e-5 and 8e-4 of closed forms). Relaxation-zone blending weights (exponential and polynomial, exact endpoints, monotone) and sponge profiles. A 1-D linear shallow-water tank for reflection estimates. Linear dispersion limits, energy equipartition and mean flux, continuity and Laplace pass; the Stokes formulas satisfy both free-surface conditions through second order (the residual is third order: ratio 8.00 for halved amplitude). 1-D toy tank: rigid wall R = 1.00000, exponential relaxation beach of 2 wavelengths R = 2.6e-4 (limit 0.05, acceptance statement met only in this toy, not in a free-surface solver). KNOWN MISSES (ignored tests, limits not changed): The registered W3 residual-scaling statement divided by the amplitude and so cannot pass (corrected test w3b passes). The registered 'abrupt zone reflects at least 0.5' check measured 0.214 (wrong premise; a post-hoc corrected comparison is labelled as such in the ADR addendum). Missing (why partial): The full tank acceptance beyond the coarse 2-D checks of wave 28A. Third and higher order Stokes, cnoidal and stream-function waves. Directional spectra. Piston/flap wave makers. Any 2-D/3-D reflection measurement. Second-order Stokes, JONSWAP and the blending formula citations are UNVERIFIED (docs/reference-data.md); the formulas are validated by the tests. Previous scope text: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv. Wave boundary conditions for the free-surface solver. WAVE 25B (ADR 0044): damping diagnosed as per-step multiplication; the sponge R=0.135 is exp(-2 int sigma dx/c); the W7(d) premise (abrupt zone reflects >= 0.5) is ill-posed for the registered blend (R=0.214); w7d stays ignored, continuum estimate misses its 25 percent limit (ignored w8_4 known miss).

title: Population balance and polydispersed phases: discrete size bins and moment methods with breakup and coalescence kernels
acceptance: Constant-kernel coalescence matches the analytic Smoluchowski moment solution
note: Priority P4. Size L. Area: fv. The audit of 2026-10-21 marks the item DONE on the acceptance text as written; scope beyond it, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed. Wave 23C delivered a LIBRARY only, one-way, with no multiphase base. Single item replaces the separate population-balance and polydispersed scope. Wave 23C (ADR 0041), partial: LIBRARY only, one-way, no multiphase base (F-127 todo). Delivered in rcfd-fv popbal.rs: 0-D fixed-pivot bins (coalescence: constant, sum, product, Brownian, shear, Saffman-Turner; breakup: constant/power rate with binary, uniform, symmetric-beta daughters). QMOM (Wheeler, located realizability errors). A one-way transport helper carrying the bins as passive scalars (no interphase coupling). Constant-kernel Smoluchowski moments matched to 1e-8 or better (bins and QMOM); sum, product and breakup closed forms and conservation to round-off checked. Gaps: case-tree wiring, interphase momentum/mass/volume-fraction coupling, turbulence-driven kernels from a k-epsilon run, DQMOM, method of classes, spatial moment transport. DONE (audit 2026-10-21, docs/audit/partials-group-*.md): acceptance text as written is met by passing tests; scope beyond the acceptance text, and the caveats in the audit file, are not claimed.

title: Six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body dynamics: force and moment integration, per-axis constraints, springs, coupling modes, user-property hook, coupled to mesh motion
acceptance: Free fall with a prescribed linear drag law reaches the analytic terminal velocity within 2 percent; a body on a prescribed spring and damper recovers the damped-oscillator frequency within 2 percent; compound pendulum period matches the closed form; locked axes stay fixed
note: Priority P2. Size M. Area: fv,mesh. DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance reworded to the prescribed drag law and prescribed spring that the tests use. The flow-coupled free fall and spring-mounted body are NOT delivered and are tracked in F-244. Merged from two proposals. WAVE 20B (ADR 0033, partial): six-degree-of-freedom rigid body (crates/rcfd-fv/src/sixdof.rs): force and moment integration on chosen patches, quaternion orientation, translation locks, locked / free / about-axis / hinge rotation, gravity, translational and torsional spring and damper, user force hook and drag hook (library), RK4 and Newmark integrators, loose explicit coupling to the moving mesh, `dynamic_mesh.motion = six_dof` in the case tree. Measured: Free flight 1e-10. Spring oscillator Newmark 1.3e-3 (limit 2e-3, order 2.0) and RK4 2.1e-6 (order 3.97). Terminal velocity with drag 2.4e-7 (1e-5). Torque-free angular momentum and energy 1e-11. Compound pendulum period 8.9e-5 (1e-3) and 4.3e-10 at amplitude 1 (RK4). Locked axes exactly fixed. Plate on a fluid layer decays with the Couette force (0.9988 of the closed form). Piston pushing a fluid column 1.00003 of the closed form. Not done: the flow-coupled spring-mounted body frequency (2 percent) and a free fall with drag in a resolved flow (the drag validation uses a registered drag hook, not a flow), strong coupling and added-mass stabilisation, free 3D rotation with Newmark, contact and multi-body, `mesh_motion = none`. DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance reworded to the prescribed drag law and prescribed spring that the tests use (R1 1.13e-10 vs 1e-8, R3 trajectory 2.4e-7 vs 1e-5, R5 pendulum 8.9e-5 / 4.3e-10 RK4, R6 locked axes exact). Correction: the '2.4e-7' above labelled terminal velocity is the damped-oscillator (R3) number; the free fall is 1.13e-10. The flow-coupled free fall and spring-mounted body are NOT delivered and are tracked in F-244.

title: Dynamic mesh layering and local remeshing, with displacement-diffusion stiffness variants
acceptance: Piston in a closed cylinder reproduces isentropic compression p V^gamma within 2 percent; volume and mass are conserved through layer add and remove
note: Priority P3. Size L. Area: mesh,fv. DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance met as written at peak piston Mach 0.05, i.e. near quasi-static. Unmet scope (local remeshing, unstructured/prism layering, case-tree/CLI wiring, incompressible layering, moving-face characteristic BCs, mesh-speed time step) moved to F-247. Separate from rigid-body motion so each can be scheduled alone. WAVE 38C (ADR 0090, partial): Layering for a structured planar layer stack with one moving piston plane (rcfd-mesh layering.rs: removal below 0.4 h0, split above 1.6 h0 into h0 plus the rest, cell source map and conservative remap). An opt-in ALE step for the explicit compressible solver (CompressibleSolver::step_ale: Galilean face-frame flux, moving slip-wall mirror, swept-volume mesh speed, GCL-consistent SSP-RK stage volumes). An InverseVolume(k) displacement-diffusion stiffness. Measured: Piston in a closed cylinder (compression ratio 2.5 and back, peak piston Mach 0.05, 24 layer removals and 24 additions) p_bar V^gamma within 1.5e-5 at full compression and 3.4e-5 after re-expansion (limit 2e-2). Volume, mass and energy conserved through every layer event to 4.4e-16. Mass drift over the run 5.4e-13. Uniform flow on a moving mesh preserved to 4.5e-15 (GCL). Inverse-volume stiffness cuts the smallest-cell strain to 0.18 of the Laplacian value (continuous 1-D 0.17). Not delivered: local remeshing, layering of unstructured or prism layers, case-tree or CLI wiring, layering in the incompressible PIMPLE path, ALE with characteristic boundary conditions on moving faces, mesh-speed-aware time step. DONE (decision 2026-10-21): acceptance met as written (p V^gamma 1.5e-5 / 3.4e-5 vs 2e-2; per-event volume, mass and energy change 4.4e-16 vs 1e-13; mass drift 5.4e-13 vs 1e-12) at peak piston Mach 0.05, i.e. near quasi-static. Unmet scope above (local remeshing, unstructured/prism layering, case-tree/CLI wiring, incompressible layering, moving-face characteristic BCs, mesh-speed time step) moved to F-247.

title: Partitioning strategies and reordering: graph partitioner, coordinate-bisection variants, radial and circumferential partitioning, node weighting, partition smoothing, reverse Cuthill-McKee reordering
acceptance: Balance within 5 percent on reference meshes for 2 to 16 parts; edge-cut of the graph partitioner not worse than coordinate bisection; reordering reduces matrix bandwidth on a stretched mesh
note: Downgraded from done to partial by user decision (2026-10-16): library and CLI only, the solver does not use partitions. Priority P3. Size S. Area: mesh,linalg. Extension of a finished partitioner trait. WAVE 15B (ADR 0020), status DONE at library level. rcfd-mesh partition: Bisection { Longest, Cycle, Fixed(axis), Inertial } with optional cell weights. Sectors { Radial, Circumferential } about an axis. GraphPartitioner (RCB-seeded greedy gain-driven boundary refinement under a balance cap; not multilevel). smooth_partition. edge_cut / weighted_imbalance helpers. rcfd-linalg reorder: rcm_order (reverse Cuthill-McKee, pseudo-peripheral start), bandwidth, CsrMatrix::bandwidth and permute_symmetric. Measured (tests partition_strategies.rs, reorder.rs): Worst unit-weight imbalance 0.030 over 8 strategies x 3 meshes x n = 2..16 (limit 0.05), worst weighted imbalance 0.0296 (control: unweighted RCB 0.613). Graph cut <= RCB cut in all 45 cases (guaranteed by construction: the unit-weight seed is RCB and every move lowers the cut; the evidence of the refinement is the 31 strict reductions, e.g. 167 to 117, 598 to 511). Smoothing restores a perturbed slab exactly (10 moves, cut 50). RCM bandwidth 72 against natural 320 on a 40x8x8 box (derived bound 127; bandwidth depends on connectivity only, so a graded mesh of the same index space gives the same numbers) and 7 against 40 on 40x6x1 (bound 11). Permutation identity error 3e-16. Not done: no multilevel coarsening, nothing is wired into the case file, CLI, solvers or GUI, and no Mesh renumbering (the ordering is a library facility so solver results and baseline hashes are unchanged). WAVE 16W (ADR 0021): wired through the case tree (`decomposition` section: bisection, inertial, sectors, graph, weights box, smoothing, reorder report, `write_field` adds the cell array `partition` to solution.vtu), `rcfd partition ... --json` (per-part cells and weights, imbalance, edge cut, ghost cells, bandwidths) and the service method `mesh.partition`, with located validation errors. The solver does not use partitions or the ordering (a report and a VTK field only); no MCP tool.

title: User-function hook catalogue v2: scalar and vector profiles, material-property, energy, species and turbulence source hooks, initialise, adjust, execute-at-end and exit hooks, reaction-rate and wall-heat-flux hooks, dynamic-zone motion, particle hooks
acceptance: Each hook, set to a constant or analytic function, reproduces the matching built-in setting or closed-form solution (property hook equals constant-property run; heat-source hook equals the slab profile)
note:
Priority P2. Size L. Area: api. Partial (wave 38A, ADR 0088). NOT delivered: turbulence source, species (multicomponent) source, adjust, a separate exit hook, reaction rate, dynamic-zone motion, specific heat and density hooks, any hook in the compressible, variable-density or VOF solvers. Delivered on the F-122 WebAssembly mechanism (ABI version 1, new optional exports, docs/udf-abi.md, docs/case-schema.md): temperature_profile (boundaries.

.temperature_udf, scalar boundary profile). wall_heat_flux (boundaries.

.heat_flux_udf; also wired into the CHT heat-flux path, not tested). thermal_conductivity (udf..conductivity). energy_source (udf..energy_source, W/m^3). scalar_source (scalars..source_udf, passive scalars). initial_value (udf..initialise: velocity, kinematic pressure, temperature). execute_at_end (udf..at_end, monitor udf_end_). The vector boundary profile is the existing velocity_profile. Measured (tests/udf_hooks_w38a.rs, limits registered first, all runs steady SIMPLEC): Every hook set to a constant equals its built-in counterpart with a relative difference of exactly 0 (limit 1e-9): temperature_expression, heat_flux_value, the constant-property run (physics.conductivity set to 5 in the hook run, hook returns 2), the uniform zone heat source, hook 5e3 plus zone source 5e3 against zone source 1e4 (amendment 1), the uniform scalar source, initial.velocity_expression_x plus uniform p and T (at build and after 50 iterations). The energy-source hook reproduces the slab profile (discrete identity to 1.1e-10 of the rise, limit 1e-6; linear source 2e4 x/L against the closed form 4.7e-4 at 64 cells, limit 6e-4). The heat-flux hook reproduces the linear closed form to 3.5e-13. The scalar hook reproduces its slab identity to 9.9e-15. execute_at_end is recorded once at the last step and equals the independent sum exactly. 17 misconfigurations are refused and a negative conductivity or a non-finite energy source stop the run. One set-up defect (C1 sanity scale) is kept ignored with a corrected test. Scope limits: Conductivity, energy and scalar sources act in steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC runs only (transient, coupled, frozen-flow refused). Conductivity is refused with property laws, CHT, radiation and heat_flux boundaries, energy source with CHT and radiation. Boundary hooks are evaluated once at t = 0. execute_at_end is not called when a run is stopped from outside the step (run(n) cap, run-control stop, wall clock, divergence guard). Particle hooks stay gated on the particle model (F-056 and F-128 are partial); none is offered.

title: Declarative setup-validation rule engine with categorised pre-solve diagnostics: dependency, required-object and count checks, auto-fix and warning severities
acceptance: A rule set of at least 10 dependency, required and count checks rejects each seeded invalid setup with the expected message id and accepts the benchmark registry cases; the published validation cases raise no error-level diagnostic
note: USER DECISION 2026-10-21: accepted as done on the definition in ADR 0092 (five registry cases plus validation cases a case file can express). Outside that definition: FAN-01 (code template, tracked under F-126) and the library-only SST plate tests. Registry folders still hold no case files; the set-ups live inside the test. Through the binary no error-level rule was observed to fire on its own, and no auto-fix is applied (suggestions only). Partial (acceptance partly met, scope limited). Delivered in rcfd-api `rules` with the data file crates/rcfd-api/rules/setup_rules.json (format rcfd-setup-rules v1): A strict declarative engine (conditions all/any/not, path and count tests with where, 13 operators, each-iteration, mesh context, located paths, sorted deterministic output of id/severity/category/path/message and optional fix). 21 registered rules (13 errors, 5 warnings, 3 infos; categories mesh, boundaries, materials, models, solver, output, setup). Wired into `rcfd check`, `rcfd validate`, `rcfd run` (error-level rule: exit 3 before solving; warnings: stderr and `warning` events with the rule id) and the `check` event (`rules` array). Measured (checks registered first in ADR 0031): E1 every one of the 21 rules fires with its id, severity, category and path on a seeded setup and no other error-level rule fires. E3 deterministic bytes. E4 strict loader rejects unknown keys/operators/severities/categories/versions, a rule written only as data works. E2 PARTIAL: on 66 distinct case texts (8 cases/**/*.toml, 1 documentation block, 57 extracted from the test sources) no error-level diagnostic, but one warning, SV103 (aspect ratio above the library's own threshold of 1000) on the wall-resolved mesh of a turbulence test case; the registered assertion lives in an ignored known-miss test, thresholds not changed. Limits: 12 of the 13 error rules restate checks the loaders already enforce (SV004 the turbulence initial-k derivation, SV009 the chain sequence check) and SV011 overlaps the mesh quality error, so through the binary no error-level rule was observed to fire on its own. The new diagnostics are SV101-SV105 and SV201-SV203. No auto-fix is applied (suggestions only). The acceptance wording 'accepts the benchmark registry cases' is evaluated on the TOML setups under cases/ because the registry case.json files are descriptors that do not load. User-function and component checks are not in the rule set. WAVE 39A (ADR 0092, done): the 'accepts the benchmark registry cases' and 'published validation cases' clauses are now measured by crates/rcfd-api/tests/registry_setups_w39a.rs V1: case-tree set-ups of the five registry descriptors (cavity Re 100 n 32; backward_step with the descriptor mesh built by gen::backward_step and read as a polyMesh file; flat_plate laminar Re_L 1e5 with wall layers; heated_cavity Ra 1e3; naca0012 on an O-grid warped onto the NACA 0012 thickness formula, Re 6e6, SST) plus cylinder Re 100, channel Re_tau 178.12 (SST), the wall-function channel and Sod, each through runctl::check_only (the library body of rcfd check). Limit exit 0 and 0 error-level rule diagnostics on all nine: met (0 errors; one warning, SV101 on the NACA O-grid, max non-orthogonality 80.3 deg). Reading registered in ADR 0092: 'published validation cases' = the five registry benchmarks plus the validation-test cases the case tree can express. ADR 0092 amendments 1-2 add V2b, the parallel-plate Graetz set-up on a prescribed parabolic flow (solver.frozen_flow): exit 0, 0 rule diagnostics (the first Graetz set-up, V2, had a zero inlet velocity and is kept as an ignored known miss). Not covered: the FAN-01 case (a format! template in fan01_validation.rs, F-126) and the w33c SST plate/wall-layer library-only set-ups. The NACA O-grid is a rule-check set-up, not a lift-prediction mesh; the registry descriptors still carry no shipped case file. USER DECISION 2026-10-21: accepted as done on the definition in ADR 0092 (five registry cases plus validation cases a case file can express). Outside that definition: FAN-01 (code template, tracked under F-126) and the library-only SST plate tests. Registry folders still hold no case files; the set-ups live inside the test. KNOWN ISSUE (ADR 0191 addendum 1, observation): SV202 (info, when no boundary condition is set) says every patch takes the default "a fixed no-slip wall"; for the compressible solver a patch without a condition is a slip wall (an outlet patch extrapolates; docs/case-schema.md), so the message is wrong there. USER DECISION 2026-11-06: the message becomes solver-aware; the change is made separately.

title: Chained run configurations: sequenced steady-then-transient restart, interpolating initial values onto a new mesh
acceptance: Two chained configurations (steady then transient restart) on the lid-driven cavity reach the same final state as a single run
note: Done under the user's reading (chain equals an uninterrupted run); the steady-then-transient chain stays covered by C1/C2. A split whose stage end clips a step by a few ulp (e.g. 0.3) is not bitwise equal and is not tested. Partial (acceptance met; scope limited). Delivered in rcfd-api `chain` and `rcfd run`: The `chain` section (sequence plus named stages with `set` overrides that accumulate, `restart` mode, transfer `method`, `allow_unconverged`). Per-stage output directories with restart files. Restart from the previous stage through the F-115 machinery (same mesh exact or steady-to-transient initialisation, changed mesh transferred). Failure propagation by exit code. Status events stage_start/restart/stage_finish/chain_finish with a `stage` field. Located static checks. Measured (checks registered first in ADR 0031): The chain's final transient state equals the manual two-run procedure bit for bit (and the CLI solution.vtu is byte-identical to `rcfd run` then `rcfd restart`). Acceptance case, 16x16 cavity steady (1e-8) then PISO dt 0.05 to t = 1: speed relative L2 distance to the single steady run 2.08e-3 and pressure (mean removed) 8.35e-3 against the registered 2e-2. 12 to 24 mesh change between stages converges (147 iterations). Failure of stage 1 gives exit 5 with stage 2 never started. Seven kinds of malformed stage definitions rejected at their located path. Threads 1 versus 3 byte-identical. Not done: operating-point sweeps (parametric-study item), chains through the service run.headless and MCP, stage-specific rule checks before the chain starts (each stage is checked as it starts), restart of transient runs with energy/scalars/turbulence, parallel or branching chains. Wave 40A (ADR 0097, test c7 in crates/rcfd-api/tests/chain_w19c.rs): two chained transient stages (PISO dt 0.05, 0 to 0.5 then exact restart to 1.0) equal one transient run from rest to t = 1 bit for bit in ux, uy, p, face flux and time (registered tolerance 0). The split at 0.5 takes ten full steps; a split whose stage end clips a step by a few ulp (e.g. 0.3) is not bitwise equal and is not tested. Done under the user's reading (chain equals an uninterrupted run); the steady-then-transient chain stays covered by C1/C2.

title: Acoustic boundary and source options: impedance boundary, non-reflecting forcing, broadband-noise estimates, wave-equation solver with sponge layers, modal export
acceptance: Impedance-tube reflection coefficient matches the closed form; a quiet boundary reflects a pulse by less than 1 percent
note: Priority P3. Size M. Area: fv,post. WAVE 32B (ADR 0066) and the job of 2026-11-12 (ADR 0233). The acceptance text is MET IN THE LIBRARY, not from a case file. Built in ADR 0233: `CompBc::Impedance { p, z }` (rcfd-fv compressible_bc.rs `impedance_wall`), a locally reacting wall with a real specific impedance on the outgoing Riemann invariant, also on moving faces; the quiet boundaries are the matched impedance `z = rho c` (holds the ambient pressure) and the existing `NonReflecting` with `sigma = 0` (holds nothing). Registered checks, all met at the first run: impedance tube with a pulse for z/(rho c) = 0, 1/3, 1, 3, 19: R within 1.13e-3 of (z - rho c)/(z + rho c) (limit 1e-2); the quiet boundaries reflect 2.1e-5 (matched) and 5.8e-8 (Thompson) of a pulse (limit 1e-2); standing-wave ratio of a tone 3.006 and 3.004 against 3 (limit 2 percent); a uniform overpressure decays to 5.4e-5 with matched walls and stays with Thompson boundaries; oblique plane pulses at 30 and 45 degrees within 1.5e-2 of (z cos - rho c)/(z cos + rho c) and of (1 - cos)/(1 + cos) (limit 3e-2). Five mutations caught. Not done: case-schema wiring (a new key needs an approved edit of case_hashes_w48u.rs; this is why the status is partial). Limits: real, frequency-independent impedance only; both quiet boundaries reflect 7 percent at 30 degrees and 17 percent at 45 degrees; gas at rest, Cartesian grids, verification against closed forms only. Unchanged from wave 32B: FW-H 1A (fwh.rs), Gutin rotor tones (rotor.rs), metrics (acoustics.rs), surface-series reader, `rcfd fwh`, non-validated broadband proxies (noise_proxies.rs), docs/acoustics.md; W5a/W5b known misses (7.7e-2 and 6.7e-2 against 1e-2 and 1e-3). Not built: wave-equation solver with sponge layers, modal export, quadrupole volume term, comparison with a measured fan, calibration of the proxy constants, on-the-fly sampling. Follow-ups (ADR 0233 questions 1, 2 and 4, recommendations taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): F-330 (wiring), F-331 (sponge layer), F-332 (frequency-dependent impedance), F-333 (wave solver and modal export). Open: question 3 (the reflection_value default reflects 46 percent of a short pulse; changing it changes a default).

title: Flow-coupled six-DOF validation: body falling through a fluid and spring-mounted body in a flow
acceptance: Laminar incompressible PISO/PIMPLE on a moving mesh, existing loose coupling (ADR 0033 D7), added-mass-to-body-mass ratio <= 0.2 (from the ADR closed form, not the displaced-fluid mass), no cyclic faces carrying a moving-wall velocity. (a) Falling body: a rigid block falling under gravity minus buoyancy along a closed 2-D channel, the displaced fluid returning through the two side gaps (falling-piston viscometer), reaches the terminal velocity of the lubrication closed form derived in the ADR within 2 percent after an approach of at least 5 time constants that fits inside the F-063 smoothing compression limit; the ADR bounds the neglected end-effect, finite-Reynolds and finite-length terms to <= 0.5 percent before the run. (b) Spring-mounted body: free decay of a spring-mounted piston driving a fluid column (the C2 geometry plus a spring, amplitude <= 1 percent of L0) oscillates at omega = sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) within 2 percent, with parameters chosen so the fluid lowers the frequency by at least 4 times the tolerance (mass ratio 0.2 gives 8.7 percent), so the check fails with fluid forces off. Both: halving dt changes the measured quantity by <= 0.5 percent; per-step continuity <= 1e-10 and the uniform-flow GCL to round-off are asserted (not only printed); in (b) the amplitude at successive same-side turning points never grows (ratio <= 1 + 1e-3; the open outlet makes body + spring + fluid energy rise during inflow by -1/2 rho A v^3, which cancels over a full period, so energy is not compared mid-cycle). Out of scope: strong (implicit) coupling and added-mass stabilisation (mass ratio > 0.2), comparison with published falling-sphere or falling-cylinder experiments or wall-correction tables (no source read), cross-flow vortex-induced vibration, free 3-D rotation with Newmark, contact and multi-body, turbulence or energy on moving meshes.
note: Split from F-229 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit; ADR 0033 reads these two clauses as flow-coupled and not delivered). Uses the moving-mesh path (F-063, partial). Size M. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): the lead's text had no named case and no closed form for 'terminal velocity with drag from the flow' or 'added mass included'. (a) now names a falling block whose drag comes from fluid displaced past it (not the tangential Couette shear of C1) with a lubrication closed form derived in the ADR. (b) now names a spring-mounted piston-column (C1/C2 are the existing flow-coupled checks; the new cases must differ and must fail without the fluid, hence the 4x frequency-shift requirement). Added a dt-halving check (moving meshes run implicit Euler only). Added asserted continuity and GCL (the F-063 audit found continuity printed but not asserted). Added an amplitude non-growth check at same-side turning points (energy injection is how explicit coupling fails; a mid-cycle energy bound would be wrong because the C2 outlet is open). The 0.2 bound is on added mass, which for a block pushing fluid through narrow gaps far exceeds its displaced mass. The lead's 'needs strong coupling or added-mass stabilisation' holds only above mass ratio 0.2 (ADR 0033 D7). PROPOSED SPLIT: strong (implicit) fluid-structure coupling with added-mass stabilisation as its own item (a feature, not a validation), with a mass-ratio >= 1 version of (b) as its acceptance. OPEN QUESTION: the title's 'spring-mounted body in a flow' is read as free decay in still fluid; a cross-flow (vortex-induced vibration) case would need a published data set chosen by the user. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split as proposed; "in a flow" is read as free decay in still fluid (no VIV case). Strong coupling is F-251. DONE (ADR 0211, the registration of F-244, 2026-11-07, branch f244-six-dof-validation, not merged): every registered check is met by library tests (crates/rcfd-fv/tests/sixdof_flow_f244.rs, test code only, no library or schema change); the acceptance is still the maintainer's. (a) A block 4 h wide and 500 h tall falling in a closed 2-D channel (gaps h) reaches 1.00545 of the lubrication terminal velocity (M - rho V_b) g / C, C = 2 mu H_b dz (3 B^2 + 1)/h, after 10 time constants (limit 2 %; added-mass ratio 0.178 from the closed form, Re_U 0.1, travel 0.42 h, smallest cell volume 0.916 of its start against the F-063 limit 0.5). The neglected terms were bounded to 0.46 % before the run: the end effect to [0, 0.363 %] by the minimum-dissipation theorem (lubrication is a lower bound of the Stokes drag; an explicit trial field gives the upper bound), inertia and finite time to 0.10 %. Halving dt changes it by 3.4e-6; the drag of a block whose sides did not move is 21 % off (negative control). (b) The C2 piston on a spring (mass ratio 0.2, amplitude 0.01 L0) oscillates at 1.0013 of sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) (limit 2 %), dt halving 2e-4; with the fluid force off it is 9.5 % off; successive same-side turning points decay by 4.7 % per period at T/100 (the lag of the explicit coupling), never grow. Both: continuity at most 3.9e-11 per step (limit 1e-10), discrete GCL 6.5e-16 mean(V), a uniform flow on both moving meshes stays uniform to 4.2e-15; four library mutations each made their checks fail. Found, not fixed (ADR 0211 amendment 1): the baseline PISO step is unstable on the block-in-channel mesh above a time step between tau/40 and tau/20 (cell diffusion number 3 to 6 across the gap), on a fixed mesh as well; the registered tau/10 run is kept as an ignored known miss and (a) runs at tau/40 and tau/80. Open: ADR 0211 Q1 (approval of the refined acceptance text), Q2 (a case-tree version), Q3 (status), Q4 (a new item for the PISO time-step limit).

title: Particle models: droplet evaporation (d-squared law) and breakup
acceptance: Two parts, each gated on its own. (A1) a single droplet evaporating in quiescent hot gas follows the quasi-steady d^2 law with the evaporation constant derived in the ADR from the registered model, measured d^2 slope within 2 percent, and the droplet mass lost equals the vapour mass source delivered to the carrier to 1e-10 relative; (A2) the breakup model reproduces its own analytic breakup time and child-size relation for a drop given a step relative velocity within 2 percent, with liquid mass conserved through breakup to round-off (critical Weber number and model constants read from the source); Out of scope: spray penetration against data (F-252), wall film (F-253), wall interaction (F-254), dispersion and reactions (F-255), group and file injections (F-056 scope).
note: Split from F-128 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). Depends on F-128 and F-056 (partial: no cyclone case). Size L. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The lead's text gated only spray and film against data while the title also lists breakup, erosion and rough-wall interaction. Each sub-model now has a closed-form or self-consistency check (d^2 law, model breakup time, impact-flux identity, rebound-distribution KS) plus a mass-conservation check, so the code can be verified before any data set is chosen. The Nusselt thickness is derived from the steady incline film profile (u = g sin(theta)/nu (delta y - y^2/2)), not cited. 'Track files' dropped: particles.tracks / particle_tracks.csv was delivered in wave 21C. PROPOSED SPLIT (this is three items, not one): spray = A (breakup, evaporation, heat/mass transfer; A3 needs a variable-density carrier with energy, a vapour species and two-way mass/energy exchange, which should be confirmed before scheduling and may itself be a fourth item since it alone is data-dependent); wall film = B; wall interaction = C (erosion, rough-wall rebound). OPEN QUESTIONS: which public vaporising-spray data set (not yet identified or read); dispersion from turbulence-model fields and particle reactions were in F-128's not-delivered list and are now tracked nowhere; should 'track files' mean something beyond particle_tracks.csv. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split into four items plus dispersion and reactions: F-252 (A3), F-253 (B), F-254 (C), F-255. This item keeps A1 and A2, verifiable without a data set. DONE (ADR 0224, the registration of F-245, 2026-11-08, branch f245-droplet, not merged): every registered check is met in the library (rcfd-particles, no case key); the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0224 Q1). (A1) Evaporation (rcfd_particles::evaporation, Tracker::set_evaporation): the quasi-steady film model with Bird's correction (model B of Both, Mira and Lehmkuhl, arXiv:2201.02818, read), Ranz-Marshall Nu and Sh, Clausius-Clapeyron through the boiling point; d^2 linear and one exponential Euler step of the temperature per sub-step (its fixed point is the wet bulb); the vapour booked per cell. The evaporation constant K = 8 rho D ln(1 + B_M(T_wb))/rho_l was derived in the ADR (3.4196739796e-7 m^2/s for the test inputs): the d^2 slope of a droplet at its wet bulb in still 800 K gas is within 1.1e-15 of K, of one injected at 300 K within 7.1e-12 after the heat-up (limit 2 percent); the vapour equals the liquid lost to 2.9e-16 for the droplet and 3.0e-12 in a spray of 160 parcels with breakup (limit 1e-10). (A2) TAB breakup (rcfd_particles::breakup, Tracker::set_breakup) with the constants and the numerical method read in O'Rourke and Amsden, LA-UR-87-2105 (1987) (C_F = 1/3, C_k = 8, C_d = 5, C_b = 1/2, K = 10/3, We_crit = 6): the breakup time arccos(1 - 12/We)/omega and the product radius r/(4/3 + We/6) of a drop at rest in a step relative velocity are reproduced to 1.5e-14 at We 6.1 to 1000 (limit 2 percent), a viscous drop to equal bits, the source's limits (eqs. 12a, 13, 16, 23) within 0.82 percent; n d^3 through breakup to 3.9e-16 and liquid plus vapour against the injected mass to 8.8e-16 in the spray. Five negative controls held, eleven mutations made their checks fail, no amendment; defaults unchanged (the particle suites of rcfd-particles and rcfd-api, H1, baseline hashes). New State::Evaporated. Open: ADR 0224 Q1 (acceptance), Q2 (case-tree wiring, recommended with F-252), Q3 (two-way exchange of mass, heat and momentum), Q4 (chi-squared product sizes), Q5 (boiling), Q6 (Abramzon-Sirignano), Q7 to Q9.

title: Pressure-interpolation variants for poor meshes
acceptance: Pressure-interpolation variants: the set of variants is named in the ADR before the work; on an incompressible manufactured solution (per-cell momentum source) on the F-208 skewed, warped and stretched meshes at n = 16, 32, 64, each variant's finest-pair L2 order is >= 1.7 for velocity and >= a pressure limit registered in the ADR, and on the near-orthogonal meshes no variant raises the error over the default by more than 1.10x (the F-208 M3 limit); a body-force-weighted variant, if named, cuts the spurious velocity of a quiescent stably stratified Boussinesq box on the skewed mesh by at least 10x against the default, below an absolute bound registered in the ADR. Out of scope: new gradient schemes, limiter changes, a separate warped-face correction (dropped, see the note), compressible-solver interpolation, automatic option selection by mesh quality, case-tree wiring (F-256).
note: Split from F-208 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). F-208 is done (ADR 0098 M5: stretched-mesh 32 -> 64 order 1.908 for C0/C1/C2), so the earlier remark that F-208 stays partial is obsolete and removed. Size M. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The phrase 'each implemented variant' was unbounded, so the ADR must name the set first. F-208's MMS exercises the scalar diffusion gradient, not pressure interpolation, so (A) needs the incompressible MMS harness ADR 0016 D2 said was missing, plus a stratified-box test where body-force weighting matters. (B) must show an error reduction, because ADR 0016 states the existing face correction already is the warped-face treatment and found it raised the error constant 2.1x on the skewed mesh, so 'does not degrade the order' alone is vacuous. (C) uses the usual wiring checks. PROPOSED SPLIT: A (M, SIMPLE kernel work) stays as F-246; C as its own S item covering the existing GradientOptions (it can ship before A); B decided by the user. OPEN QUESTION: is a separate warped-face correction wanted at all, given ADR 0016 D2 treats the corrected face gradient as the warped-face treatment? USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split: case-tree wiring is F-256; the separate warped-face correction (B) is dropped because ADR 0016 D2 already treats the corrected face gradient as the warped-face treatment and found the correction raised the error constant 2.1x on the skewed mesh; reopen only if A shows a warped-mesh residual. PARTIAL (ADR 0193, the registration of F-246, 2026-11-06, branch f246-pressure-interp, not merged): The set named before the work, on the steady simple/simplec kernel: linear (the default), skew_corrected (the Green-Gauss face pressure moved to the face centre with the interpolated cell gradient) and body_force_weighted (the same discretisation applied to the pressure minus a local potential of the body force: in the Green-Gauss face pressures, the wall pressures, the least-squares gradients of the non-orthogonal correction and the body-force part of the face flux). Case key solver.pressure_interpolation, left out of the settings hash at its default, wired under F-256's checks: located errors, tree equals library exactly (0, limit 1e-12), the default unchanged bit for bit. Met: the stably stratified Boussinesq box on the skewed mesh K at n = 16: body_force_weighted cuts the largest spurious cell speed from 1.6e-2 to 3.7e-12 (SIMPLEC with face_flux) and from 4.6e-3 to 1.0e-11 (SIMPLE with one corrector); limits 10x and 1e-6 (1e-8 of the buoyancy velocity 100). skew_corrected keeps the velocity error on the near-orthogonal meshes at 1.000 (G) and 1.0015 (G3) times the default's (limit 1.10). Met on the manufactured flow (orders of the pair (32, 64), limits 1.7 velocity and 1.2 pressure): skewed mesh K, skew_corrected 2.176 / 1.491 and body_force_weighted 2.235 / 1.444; stretched mesh S, body_force_weighted 1.966 / 1.318, skew_corrected 1.735 / 1.756. The n = 64 sequences take about two hours each and are ignored heavy tests run by name. Missed (ignored *_known_miss tests, limits unchanged): the default kernel diverges on F-208's warped mesh W from n = 32 under every set-up tried (relaxation, viscosity, convection scheme, correctors, pseudo-time, face_flux, SIMPLEC); skew_corrected and body_force_weighted diverge there too, so M1 on W is not met; amendment 1 added a milder warp W2 (amplitude 0.07, 45 degrees) as supplementary evidence, on which both variants meet the limits (skew_corrected 1.999 / 1.745, body_force_weighted 1.999 / 1.648); body_force_weighted raises the velocity error on the near-orthogonal meshes 1.342 (G) and 1.150 (G3) times (limit 1.10): it assumes the pressure balances the body force, and the manufactured source does not. Amendment 1 also corrected the stratified-box set-up B-a (SIMPLEC at alpha_p = 1 without correctors diverged for both variants) by adding face_flux. Open (ADR 0193 Q1 to Q9): the key's name, the transient kernel, the rotating-frame sources, the readings of the acceptance, the default, the wiring, further variants, W2 as the warped mesh, and whether the divergence on W reopens the dropped warped-face item. USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0193 decision record): stays PARTIAL; W stays the binding warped mesh and W2 is supplementary evidence only (Q8 (a)); amendment 1 and the heavy tests run by hand are accepted as evidence; the divergence on W is the new item F-285 (Q9 (b)), after which M1 on W is run again unchanged; the R2 cases of T1 are redone by the house rule, separately. Q1 to Q7 were not asked and stay open.

title: Dynamic mesh: local remeshing on unstructured tetrahedral meshes
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Local remeshing: the ADR 0090 piston in a closed cylinder on an unstructured tetrahedral mesh, with remeshing instead of layering, keeps p_bar V^gamma within 2e-2 at full compression and after re-expansion, conserves volume, mass, momentum and energy through every remeshing event to 1e-13 relative (conservative remap), triggers at least 5 events, and keeps the minimum cell quality above the ADR threshold. Out of scope: sliding interfaces / AMI (F-250), elastic-analogy smoothing (F-063), six-DOF coupling (F-244), more than one moving layered boundary, non-planar layer surfaces, turbulence or energy in the incompressible moving-mesh path.
note: Split from F-230 on 2026-10-21 (partials audit). Depends on F-063 (partial). Size L. REFINED 2026-10-21 (not yet user-approved): The lead's text bundled six sub-scopes under one unnamed 'closed-form or benchmark result' and asked for incompressible case-tree selectability, which already exists for prescribed and six-DOF motion (ADR 0033 D8, T1-T4); what is missing is wiring of layering and compressible ALE. Each part now has a named case reusing a registered closed form (ADR 0090 piston p V^gamma, ADR 0033 G5 piston flux) plus conservation checks. ADR 0098's Mach 0.2 piston passed with the |u| + c time step but did not deliver the mesh-speed time step; it stays in (C). PROPOSED SPLIT: remeshing = A (L); layering extensions = B (M); compressible ALE boundaries and time step = C (S to M); wiring = D (S, can ship first). OPEN QUESTION: should more than one moving layered boundary (in ADR 0090's not-delivered list) be tracked here or dropped.
