USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split four ways: B is F-257, C is F-258, D is F-259; more than one moving layered boundary is dropped as out of scope (no use case). This item keeps A (remeshing), size L. DONE (ADR 0215, the registration of F-247, 2026-11-07, branch f247-local-remeshing, not merged): every registered check is met; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0215 Q6). Library only. rcfd_mesh::remesh::TetRemesher holds a tetrahedral mesh bounded by axis-aligned planes; move_plane_with_band moves a piston plane and drags the points within 2 h0 behind it in proportion; a cell below mean ratio 0.3 or an edge outside [0.5 h0, 2 h0] triggers an event of local operators (edge split, collapse, edge removal including the 2-2 flip of a wall edge, 2-3 flip, point relocation), each checked to tile the same region; every operator gives the cell totals to the new cells by exact tetrahedron intersection volumes, and remesh::remap carries them through CompressibleSolver::replace_mesh. ADR 0090's piston on the Delaunay tetrahedral mesh M0 (1711 cells): p V^gamma 3.7e-6 at full compression and 9.4e-6 after re-expansion (limit 2e-2); 1806 events (limit 5); volume, mass, momentum and energy through every event within 1.6e-15 (1e-13); smallest mean ratio 0.241 (ADR threshold 0.2); per-step mass 7.6e-15 and volume 5.0e-15; no point below x = 0.35 touched (limit 0.2); raw intersection mismatch 5.1e-14 (1e-11); 55497 steps in 193 s. Negative controls: a largest-source remap changes the mass by 7.9e-7; without remeshing the mean ratio falls below 0.2 at t = 5.2 (T = 16). Unit checks met; four mutations failed their checks, the fifth did not and was replaced by amendment 3 (MU3': Q 0.097). Amendments before the registered runs: 1 (U2 gradual), 2 (band motion, collapse rules, boundary edge removal, from development runs on scratch set-ups). Defaults: new files and one pub mod line; baseline hashes and H1 unedited; no case-schema key. Gate of 6e7ee92: fmt 0, clippy 0, 3150 passed, 0 failed, 889 ignored. Open (ADR 0215 Q1 to Q7): case-tree wiring, the quality measure and threshold, remeshing in the incompressible path, non-planar walls, a higher-order remap, the status, a panic of the existing mesher seen while choosing M0.

title: SIMPLEC robustness: velocity inlet with a forward vent (K > 0) diverges from the first iteration
acceptance: The registered vent test x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt (pseudo-dt 0.02, u = +-0.5, +-1, +-2; outlet pressure 0.5 K u|u| within 1e-6) passes as a non-ignored test with plain SIMPLEC, without changing the default settings of existing cases (baseline hashes unchanged)
note: Size M. Done with an opt-in key (solver.simplec_boundary_compensation), accepted by the user on 2026-10-22; making the key the default is NOT approved. The default-code X7 test still gives NaN at u = 2, and with the key plain SIMPLEC with a strong vent (K = 10) still fails. Found by wave 39D (ADR 0095): plain SIMPLEC diverges from the first iteration with a velocity inlet and a forward vent when K > 0; X7 gave NaN at u = 2 and is an ignored known miss. User decision 2026-10-21: fix in the next foundations wave with the SIMPLEC seam-compensation defect. WAVE 41B (ADR 0102): DONE with an opt-in key. Root cause (diagnosed by registered switch runs): SIMPLEC added the flux compensation (rAtU - rAU) snGrad(p_old) on internal faces only, so a change of the vent pressure kicked the vent-cell velocity by (rAtU - rAU) times the pressure jump (5.06 m/s in the first plain iteration at u = 1, 1.125 at u = 2 with pseudo-time 0.02). The vent law, which reads that velocity, fed it back with the gain G = 0.5 (rAtU - rAU) (A/V) K |u|. The run diverges when G > 1 (10.1 plain, 1.125 at u = 2, pseudo 0.02), not by Courant number (K = 1 at Courant 2 settles, K = 10 at Courant 1 diverges). Inlet treatment and seams play no role in X7; a face-velocity vent law is not a cure (it diverges through a transverse mode). Fix: solver.simplec_boundary_compensation (default false, bit-identical; steady simplec only, located error otherwise; docs/case-schema.md) adds the compensation on fixed-pressure and periodic boundary faces, so the fixed point equals SIMPLE's (B1 pressure outlet 3.5e-12, B2 periodic seams 4.7e-13 against default differences 4.8e-3 and 2.6e-3; the same key addresses ADR 0084 finding S (seams), opt-in). Acceptance: x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt (crates/rcfd-api/tests/heat_exchanger.rs, non-ignored) is the registered X7 sweep with the one added line simplec_boundary_compensation = true: worst error 2.93e-12 (limit 1e-6) at all six flows; the default-code x7_vent_at_fixed_pseudo_dt_known_miss stays ignored and still gives NaN at u = 2; baseline hashes unchanged. Reading of the acceptance: 'plain SIMPLEC' = the simplec algorithm with this one opt-in key; the default settings of existing cases are unchanged. Also: X7 without pseudo-time settles with the key (errors <= 6.4e-13). Remains: with the key, plain SIMPLEC with a strong vent (K = 10) still fails through a transverse vent-face mode (F-200 C3 channel non-finite at iteration 2767), pseudo-time needed there; the key is not the default because it changes every converged SIMPLEC result with a pressure boundary or periodic seam; the FAN-01 residual stall is not caused by the missing compensation (ADR 0102 R3, falsified). USER DECISION 2026-10-22: accepted done with the opt-in key solver.simplec_boundary_compensation. Making the key the default is NOT approved (it changes every converged SIMPLEC result with a pressure boundary or seam). Queued: a located diagnostic that suggests the key when a steady SIMPLEC run diverges. WAVE 42A (ADR 0105): the queued diagnostic is delivered. When the steady divergence guard (ADR 0077, unchanged: non-finite values, continuity growth 1e6 over the 50-iteration minimum, speed / pressure runaway) stops a steady SIMPLEC run whose case has a fixed-pressure or periodic boundary face and solver.simplec_boundary_compensation is false, the run-control reason and service error append a hint naming solver.simplec_boundary_compensation = true (only Simulation::steady_divergence_message, read-only; other algorithms and texts unchanged; defaults unchanged). Tests in rcfd-api tests/heat_exchanger.rs: d1 (X7 vent u = 2, pseudo 0.02, no key: diverged at iteration 9, reason names the key; limit 15); d1n (diverging SIMPLE cavity: no hint); d2 (X7 vent u = 0.5 converging, 600 iterations bit-identical with and without querying the message every iteration).

title: Parametric studies, remaining scope: multi-objective optimiser, Nelder-Mead robustness, warm start beyond steady SIMPLE/SIMPLEC
acceptance: A multi-objective study over at least two design parameters returns a Pareto set verified against a known analytic front within a limit registered in an ADR; the Nelder-Mead optimiser reaches the registered T3 target; a warm-started sweep point reproduces its cold-started result within a registered tolerance
note: Split from F-095 on 2026-10-21 (wave 40C, ADR 0099). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. Size L. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: split: CMA-ES and the real-fan study are F-260 (blocked on FAN-01 convergence). This item keeps the analytic clauses.

title: Sliding interface (AMI): arbitrary mesh interface between non-conforming moving or rotating zones
acceptance: A rotor-stator case with a sliding interface, the mesh sliding by at least one full cell pitch, conserves mass across the interface to 1e-10 relative per step summed over all interface faces; rigid rotation of a fluid across the interface differs from the same case on a conforming mesh by no more than 1.5 times the conforming-mesh velocity error; a Taylor-Couette torque across the interface is within 2 percent of the closed form; a case without the interface is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged)
note: Split from F-063 on 2026-10-21 (user decision after the F-063 audit). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. F-114 handles planar interfaces only; F-126 covers frozen-rotor and mixing-plane. Size L. USER DECISION 2026-10-22: acceptance tightened with numeric limits (the 1.5x ratio and 2 percent are fixed here; refine only with the user). ADR 0216 (registration of F-250, 2026-11-07, branch f250-sliding-interface, not merged): PARTIAL, library only. Built: a rotor block turns against a stator block across a cylinder and the interface is rebuilt every step (rcfd_mesh::sliding, rcfd_fv::sliding, PimpleSolver::step_sliding); the mesh flux of the interface faces closes the GCL of the interface slivers, and the old flux is projected onto the new faces. Met: rigid rotation (A2) 5.94e-4 against 1.5 x the static conforming controls (8.90e-4), and the equal-count cell difference 2.36e-4 against 8.63e-4; Taylor-Couette torque (A3) on the rotor wall +1.41 %, on the stator wall -1.34 %, through the interface -0.10 % (limit 2 %); uniform flow held to 9e-15 (2-D) and 4e-15 (3-D); the decaying azimuthal mode at -0.41 % of nu k^2 (closed form); a case without the interface unchanged (no tree change). A1 missed as registered (two non-orthogonal correctors): interface mass 1.51e-10 against 1e-10, the lagged non-orthogonal flux; met with six correctors (amendment 2): 3.0e-15. Other known misses: continuity 1.8e-9 to 1.7e-8 with two correctors (limit 1e-9), and R1b against rotating conforming controls (the static stator wall's pressure condition). Not delivered: the case-tree, CLI and Studio wiring (ADR 0216 Q1); planar and sector sliding (Q3); a flow check that sees the rotor mesh flux (Q7).

title: Strong (implicit) fluid-structure coupling with added-mass stabilisation
acceptance: A spring-mounted piston driving a fluid column at an added-mass to body-mass ratio of at least 1 oscillates at omega = sqrt(k/(M + rho A L0)) within 2 percent, the amplitude at successive same-side turning points never grows (ratio <= 1 + 1e-3) over at least 10 periods, and the explicit coupling of ADR 0033 D7 grows or diverges on the same case (registered before the run); halving dt changes the frequency by <= 0.5 percent
note: Split from F-244 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. Size L. Needed for light structures; not on the first fan path.

title: Spray penetration of a vaporising spray against a public data set
acceptance: liquid and vapour penetration of a constant-volume vaporising spray within 10 percent of a public data set chosen by the user, values read from the source and registered in an ADR before the run. Needs a variable-density carrier with energy, a vapour species and two-way mass and energy exchange; confirm before scheduling.
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Blocked on the choice of a public vaporising-spray data set (not yet identified or read) and on the carrier physics. Size L.

title: Particle wall film (Nusselt thickness, mass conservation)
acceptance: Wall film: a laminar film fed by impinging parcels on an inclined wall reaches the Nusselt thickness derived in the ADR, delta = (3 mu Gamma / (rho^2 g sin(theta)))^(1/3) with Gamma the mass flow per unit width, within 5 percent at a station away from the feed, at a film Reynolds number inside the laminar range registered in the ADR; film + airborne + escaped parcel mass conserved to 1e-10 relative. Out of scope: comparison with measured data beyond the stated data set, particle reactions, discrete-element coupling.
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0192, the registration of F-253, 2026-11-05, branch f253-wall-film, not merged): every registered check is met; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0192 Q1). A thin laminar film lives on the faces of wall patches (rcfd_particles::film; the optional table particles.film with enabled, patches and viscosity, absent from every existing case). A parcel that reaches it is absorbed (state film). The film moves down the wall with the lubrication velocity rho h^2 g_t/(3 mu) by donor-cell fluxes under a Courant limit on the kinematic wave, and drains at open edges. On a 30-degree incline fed by four parcel streams at Re_f = 4 Gamma/mu = 2 (laminar range 0 to 30, long-wave threshold 5.77 at 30 degrees), the station six rows below the feed is within 2.6e-15 of the Nusselt thickness as a window average and 1.7e-11 at 20 s (limit 5 percent); injected = airborne + deposited + escaped + stuck + film + drained to 6.1e-13 (limit 1e-10). The case tree, with gravity tilted instead of the mesh, gives 1.7e-11 and equals the library bit for bit. Runs without the film are unchanged bit for bit (records R1 and R2, made on main before the code). The first run of the tree checks stopped at a set-up defect of case K (frozen flow needs energy.enabled), corrected by amendment 1 before the corrected run; the tests on the registered K stay ignored. Open: gas buoyancy is left out of the film so that its steady state is the roadmap formula (ADR 0192 Q2); gas shear (Q3) and splash or rebound at impact (Q4) are not delivered. USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0192 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q1, not closed yet); gas buoyancy and gas shear are the new item F-292 (Q2, Q3); splash and rebound at the film are the new item F-284, not part of F-254 (Q4).

title: Particle wall interaction: erosion and rough-wall rebound
acceptance: Wall interaction: for a uniform parcel stream hitting a plate at three angles, the reported erosion rate equals the closed-form impact-flux expression of the chosen correlation (constants read from the source) to 1e-10 relative; the rough-wall rebound model's sampled rebound angles match its prescribed distribution (Kolmogorov distance below the 1 percent critical value for the sample size). Out of scope: comparison with measured data beyond the stated data set, particle reactions, discrete-element coupling.
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0194, the registration of F-254, 2026-11-06, branch f254-wall-interaction, not merged): every registered check is met; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0194 Q1). Erosion (rcfd_particles::erosion; the optional table particles.erosion with enabled, patches, k, n and density, absent from every existing case) books m K U^n F(alpha) of DNV RP O501 (Revision 4.2-2007, eq. 7.1 to 7.3, constants of Table 7-1 read from the source; K and n are inputs) on each face at every parcel hit, as an observation that never changes a parcel, and reports the rate per face over the tracked time. For three uniform streams on a plate at 15, 35 and 90 degrees the reported rate equals G K U^n F(alpha) to 5.4e-13 (limit 1e-10), in the library and in the case tree. Rough walls (rcfd_particles::rough; the optional table particles.rough_wall with enabled, patches, angle_std and seed) reflect about a virtual wall tilted in the plane of incidence by a Gaussian roughness angle (Sommerfeld 1992 as restated by Tian et al. 2007), with a registered realizability rule (redraw until the parcel meets the virtual wall from the fluid side and rebounds away from the wall). The rebound angles of 20 000 parcels at 10, 40 and 75 degrees match the prescribed distribution with Kolmogorov distances 0.0047, 0.0059 and 0.0058 against the 1 percent critical value 0.0115; the untruncated Gaussian is rejected (0.27). The case tree equals the library bit for bit. Runs without the models are unchanged bit for bit (records R3 and R4, made on main before the code, and R1, R2 of ADR 0192). Open: the shadow-effect distribution of Sommerfeld and Huber (1999) was not read, so the realizability rule stands in for it (ADR 0194 Q2); K and n have no default (Q3); the DNV edition read is a third-party copy of Revision 4.2-2007 (Q4); splash and rebound at the wall film (ADR 0192 Q4) are not delivered (Q5); wall friction and particle rotation are not modelled (Q6). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0194 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q1, not closed yet); named steel presets for K, n and the target density (Q3, against the recommendation), made separately, which must say that the Table 7-2 values come from a third-party copy of DNV RP O501 Revision 4.2-2007 not checked against the maintainer's edition; Q2 (the Sommerfeld and Huber 1999 paper) and Q4 (the DNV edition) wait for the maintainer; splash and rebound at the film are the new item F-284 (Q5); Q6 was not asked.

title: Particle dispersion from turbulence-model fields and particle reactions
acceptance: Particle dispersion driven by turbulence-model fields reproduces the analytic dispersion growth of a passive cloud in homogeneous turbulence (Taylor result, closed form derived in the ADR) within 5 percent, and a particle surface reaction conserves the mass of each species to 1e-10 relative
note: Split from F-245 on 2026-10-22 (user decision): these were in F-128's not-delivered list and tracked nowhere. Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. Size L. PARTIAL (ADR 0208, the registration of F-255, 2026-11-07, branch f255-particle-dispersion, not merged): every registered check is met, the surface reaction in the library only; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0208 Q1). Dispersion: the opt-in table `particles.dispersion_from_model` (`enabled`; hash_omit_default, absent from every existing case; amendment 2 moved it out of `particles` because H1 of `case_hashes_w48u` compares the written text) makes the random walk of ADR 0057 take k and epsilon per cell from `k_epsilon` (its epsilon) or `k_omega_sst` (epsilon = 0.09 k omega), once for steady and frozen tracking and before every tracking step of a transient run (the old time level with two-way coupling); library `Tracker::set_dispersion_fields`. The closed form for a Stokes parcel released at rest (`rcfd_particles::drw_msd`, Taylor's `taylor_msd` for tau -> 0) is derived in the ADR and matches the moment equations of the walk to 7.6e-12. A cloud of 20 000 tracer parcels (tau = 1e-3 T_L) on the k-epsilon and SST models' homogeneous fields is within 0.04 to 0.79 percent of both forms at 0.25, 1, 4 and 10 T_L (limit 5 percent), an inertial cloud (tau = T_L) within 1.1 percent; the tree equals the library bit for bit on non-uniform fields, and the transient and two-way refreshes give the fields of the right time level bit for bit. Reaction (`rcfd_particles::reaction`, `Tracker::set_reaction`): a first-order kinetic surface reaction with an inert residue (a choice of the ADR, Q7), linear shrinkage to 1.7e-14, the mass of the solid and of each gas species measured on the parcel side and on the carrier side within 2.0e-14 at every step of a run with wall hits (limit 1e-10). Runs without the new keys and calls are unchanged bit for bit (records R8, R9, R1 to R7, H1, baseline hashes). Ten mutations made their checks fail; two set-up defects of checks and the place of the key were corrected by amendments 1 to 3 before the corrected runs. Open (ADR 0208 Q1 to Q10): the key; the models (RSM, SA, LES refused); C_mu of the eddy length; the homogeneous check on the model's initial state; the zero eddy held forever; the reaction law, its case keys, parcels that burn out completely and the molar masses.

title: Case-tree wiring of the gradient options
acceptance: Case-tree wiring of the existing GradientOptions (face correction, secondary limiter, boundary-gradient treatment; options added later (for example by F-246) wire under the same checks): invalid values give located errors, a tree run equals the library run with the same options to 1e-12, and a case without the keys is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged). Out of scope: new gradient schemes, limiter changes.
note: Split from F-246 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Can ship before F-246. Size S. DONE (ADR 0190, the registration of F-256, 2026-11-05, branch f256-gradient-wiring, not merged): the keys solver.gradient_face_correction, gradient_secondary_limiter (none, barth_jespersen, venkatakrishnan), gradient_limiter_k (default 5) and gradient_boundary (owner, corrected, dropped), left out of the settings hash at their defaults, set the library options of the diffusion term of the energy equation (incompressible constant-density solvers, P1 radiation included) and of the transported scalars and species. Invalid values, and options that would act on nothing (a scheme without a cell gradient, no equation that takes them, K without its limiter), are located errors (G1). On a wedge mesh of 29.6 degrees non-orthogonality the tree run equals the library run exactly (0, limit 1e-12) for seven option sets of the steady energy equation and for ADR 0016's set C2 of the transient energy equation and a poisson scalar, and each set moves the result by 2.2e-5 to 1.8e-2 against the default (G2, G3). The keys at their defaults change no bit and no settings hash; baseline hashes unchanged (G4). Open: the names and place of the keys (ADR 0190 Q1); the default K (Q2); the conjugate heat_flow report keeps the default secondary flux (Q3); the options stay off momentum, pressure, turbulence and the electric potential (Q4). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0190 decision record): the heat_flow report with the options and a balance check is the new item F-289 (Q3 (b)); the options on turbulence transport, momentum, pressure and the electric potential are the new item F-291 (Q4 (b)); Q1 and Q2 were not asked.

title: Dynamic mesh: prism layering and incompressible layering
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Layering extensions: (B1) the same piston with prism (extruded triangle) layers meets the ADR 0090 limits (p V^gamma 2e-2, per-event conservation 1e-13, mass drift 1e-12); (B2) layering in the incompressible PIMPLE path: the ADR 0033 G5 piston channel run long enough for at least 5 layer removals keeps per-step continuity <= 1e-9, outlet flux equal to the piston swept flux to 1e-10 per step and volume conserved per layer event to 1e-13. Out of scope: sliding interfaces / AMI (F-250), elastic-analogy smoothing (F-063), six-DOF coupling (F-244), more than one moving layered boundary, non-planar layer surfaces, turbulence or energy in the incompressible moving-mesh path.
note: Split from F-247 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size M. DONE (ADR 0213, the registration of F-257, 2026-11-07, branch f257-prism-layering, not merged): every registered check is met; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0213 Q5). Library only. rcfd_mesh::layering::ExtrudedStack stacks prisms over a planar cross-section (Section::rect, Section::rect_triangles) with the piston, thresholds and cell source map of LayerStack (one shared event function); face_sources and remap_face_flux carry the face flux through an event (a merged side face takes the sum of the two old faces, a split one the share of its layer height, the faces of a new plane close the cell below them); PimpleSolver::replace_mesh installs the new mesh with the remapped velocity, pressure and flux. (B1) ADR 0090's piston on 320 triangular prisms: p V^gamma 1.53e-5 at T and 3.42e-5 at 2T (limit 2e-2), per-event conservation 6.7e-16 (1e-13), mass drift 6.95e-13 (1e-12), volume 1.1e-15 (1e-13), 24 removals and 24 additions. (B2) ADR 0033 G5b mirrored in x on a layered mesh (the piston is xmax), 120 steps with 7 removals: step continuity 3.1e-15 (1e-9), outlet against the piston's swept flux 1.3e-14 (1e-10), volume per event 2.2e-16 (1e-13); with the piston pulled out, 7 additions meet the same limits. The face map's balance and uniform-flow checks hold to 9.1e-16 and 1.6e-16; replace_mesh with the same mesh changes no bit; four mutations each made their check fail; records L1 and L2, ADR 0207's R1 to R4, baseline hashes and H1 unedited. The case tree is not changed (ADR 0191 E6 and E7 stay). Observed, no limit: the cell velocity next to the piston lags by 4.7e-3 of a0 t on the layered channel (2.9e-4 on the smoothed mesh, ADR 0033's known miss of G5 (iii)). Open (ADR 0213 Q1 to Q5): the case-tree wiring under F-259, the piston end, the flux and the pressure of a split, and the status.

title: Compressible ALE boundaries and mesh-speed time step
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Compressible ALE boundaries and time step: max_dt uses |u.n - w_n| + c (checked against the closed form for a uniform gas on a mesh moving at w to round-off); uniform flow is preserved to 1e-12 with characteristic boundary faces that move; a piston-generated simple wave leaving through a moving characteristic outlet reflects with amplitude below the ADR limit. Out of scope: sliding interfaces / AMI (F-250), elastic-analogy smoothing (F-063), six-DOF coupling (F-244), more than one moving layered boundary, non-planar layer surfaces, turbulence or energy in the incompressible moving-mesh path.
note: Split from F-247 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Size S to M. PARTIAL (ADR 0207, the registration of F-258, 2026-11-07, branch f258-compressible-ale, not merged): every registered check is met in the library; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0207 Q5). On a moving face the compressible ALE step evaluates the total inlet, the pressure outlet, the non-reflecting outlet and the far field in the frame of the face (rcfd_fv::compressible::characteristic_face_state: lab-frame data, switches on the relative normal velocity, flux F(q).n - w_n U(q)); CompressibleSolver::max_dt_moving and max_dt_ale take the step with |u.n - w_n| + c (max_dt_ale with the face speeds of the last ALE step). The step of a uniform gas on a translating box equals its closed form to 2.8e-15 (limit 1e-12); a uniform flow with the four conditions on moving faces stays uniform to 1.9e-14 (limit 1e-12); a piston-generated simple wave leaves through an outlet moving at Mach 0.2 with a reflection of 4.6e-4 of its pressure jump (far field) and 3.8e-4 (non-reflecting, sigma 0) (limit 1e-2; a fixed-pressure outlet reflects 1.0); four mutations each made their check fail; max_dt() and every run without a characteristic condition on a moving face are unchanged bit for bit (R1 to R4, baseline hashes, H1). The case tree is not changed (ADR 0191 E5 stays, the tree steps with max_dt()). Open: ADR 0207 Q1 to Q4 (the tree wiring under F-259, the tree's moving step, lagged or predicted mesh speed, the frame of the total-inlet data).

title: Case-tree and CLI wiring of layering and compressible ALE
acceptance: Every limit not stated here is registered in the ADR before the run. Case-tree and CLI wiring of layering and compressible ALE (incompressible prescribed and six-DOF motion are already in the tree, ADR 0033 D8): invalid keys give located errors, a tree run equals the library run to 1e-12, and a case without the keys is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged). Out of scope: sliding interfaces / AMI (F-250), elastic-analogy smoothing (F-063), six-DOF coupling (F-244), more than one moving layered boundary, non-planar layer surfaces, turbulence or energy in the incompressible moving-mesh path.
note: Split from F-247 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Can ship first. Size S. PARTIAL (ADR 0191, the registration of F-259, 2026-11-05, branch f259-layering-ale-wiring, not merged): a transient compressible run (solver.algorithm = compressible) moves its mesh under a prescribed dynamic_mesh motion with rigid or smoothing deformation (the ALE step of ADR 0090), and dynamic_mesh.deformation = layering runs ADR 0090's planar layer stack of a piston on the new generator mesh.generator = box_3d (thresholds 0.4 and 1.6 of lx / nx, no key); no new key, defaults and the incompressible checks unchanged; invalid settings give located errors (E1 to E13; E8 and E2 also through rcfd validate, E8 with its line number), and a piston driven through the last static plane stops the run with a dynamic_mesh: message; ADR 0090's piston P (9191 steps, 24 removals and 24 additions), a smoothed piston with a static pressure outlet and a rigidly moving uniform flow give the same bits through the tree as through library calls (limit 1e-12), and rcfd run gives the reports of the in-process run; ADR 0090's limits hold on the tree run (p V^gamma 1.5e-5 at full compression and 3.4e-5 after the stroke against 2e-2, mass drift 5.4e-13 against 1e-12); fixed-mesh compressible runs are bit-identical to main (D0), baseline hashes and H1 unedited. Open: the wiring of F-257 (prism and incompressible layering) and F-258 (characteristic conditions on moving faces, the mesh-speed time step) waits for that library work, and done or partial is the maintainer's call (ADR 0191 Q3); layer thresholds are not keys (Q1); the InverseVolume smoothing stiffness is not in the tree (Q2); the Studio gives no cell estimate for box_3d (Q4). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0191 decision record): stays PARTIAL (Q3, not closed yet); inverse-volume smoothing is the new item F-290 (Q2 (b)); box_3d in the Studio's lists follows the maintainer's Studio worktree (Q4 (a), F-293); Q1 was not asked. The SV202 message observed in addendum 1 is recorded under F-240.

title: Parametric studies: CMA-ES and a real-fan study
acceptance: CMA-ES reaches the registered target on a multimodal analytic test function from a start where Nelder-Mead does not (limits registered in an ADR); a multi-objective study on the FAN-01 passage over at least two blade parameters, using a converged solver, returns a Pareto set whose members are re-run to confirm their reported objectives within 1 percent
note: Split from F-249 on 2026-10-22 (user decision). Acceptance text proposed by the lead; refine when scheduled. Blocked on FAN-01 solver convergence (waves 43B-C). Size L. PARTIAL (ADR 0222, the registration of F-260, 2026-11-08, branch f260-cmaes, not merged): the CMA-ES clause is met; the real-fan study is not attempted. Built: the opt-in method cma_es (library design::cmaes, Method::CmaEs, the design tools' {"type": "cma_es", budget, pop, sigma0, restarts, seed}): the (mu/mu_W, lambda)-CMA-ES of Hansen's tutorial (arXiv:1604.00772v2, Fig. 6, Table 1 and Appendix B read; its source-code appendix not opened), with its termination criteria, the tutorial's box rule (62) (a sample outside the box is not evaluated and ranks last) and restarts with the population doubled (Auger and Hansen 2005). Met: on the shifted Rastrigin function in 4 dimensions, from a start three local minima from the optimum in every coordinate, CMA-ES with 9 restarts reaches f <= 1e-8 within 40 000 evaluations on 20 of 20 seeds (limit 18 of 20), while Nelder-Mead from the same start (default and ADR 0209 options, 40 runs) stops in the local minimum f = 35.82; the sphere and the ellipsoid of condition 1e6 in 10 dimensions reach 1e-10 on 20 of 20 seeds; the parameters, update, eigensolver, normal draws and termination criteria against their closed forms; study, propose / record, resume and tool checks; every mutation fails its test. Recorded: 3 of 20 seeds without restarts; 14 of 20 in 10 dimensions within 100 000 evaluations (Nelder-Mead 0 of 20). Not attempted (ADR 0222 reading 2): the multi-objective FAN-01 study. FAN-01 has no converged solve (the second-order limit cycle of ADRs 0110 to 0181; the first-order example case of ADR 0176 ends not_converged at its cap), F-126 is partial, and no case key carries a scalar blade parameter (the blade is sixteen station lists). Defaults bit-identical. Open: ADR 0222 Q1 to Q5 (Q1: split the real-fan study into a new item and call F-260 done, recommended; Q2 the box rule; Q3 the defaults; Q4 the tool description; Q5 the restart points).

title: Studio project folder library (rcfd-project)
acceptance: A project is a folder with a versioned manifest, case and mesh references and immutable run records; writes are atomic, a torn file is detected, old schema versions migrate, and a file watcher reports external edits. Limits are registered in ADR 0122 and checked by headless tests.
note: Wave 47A (ADR 0122) and audit fixes in ADR 0128. Library only, no window. Size M. Not done: moving the run service onto these types (the runner keeps its own copies, to be unified), and the other additive contract items listed in the ADR addendum.

title: Studio run service (rcfd-runner)
acceptance: A detached runner owns a queue of runs under a CPU and memory budget with pause, resume, cancel and crash recovery, and reports state through append-only status files. Kill tests show a killed runner leaves no run in a false running state. Limits are registered in ADR 0123.
note: Wave 47B (ADR 0123). Size L. One registered check (S5) is an ignored known miss. Fixes in ADR 0128: no caller-chosen binary, status-write failure stops the run, liveness needs two misses, bounded output drain, argv quoting, no console window. Memory probing uses typeperf with a time limit and a 5 s PowerShell fallback. Not done: socket control (files only), runs started from the application.

title: Studio time-series field store (rcfd-tsstore)
acceptance: The mesh is stored once and field snapshots per saved time are chunked, compressed and indexed, so a reader can jump to any saved time and read it back bit-exactly. A bad tail left by a crash is tolerated. Limits are registered in ADR 0124.
note: Wave 47C (ADR 0124). Library level. Size M. Not done: residual and monitor series are not in the store yet, and the solver does not write to it.

title: Studio wgpu render core v0 (rcfd-render)
acceptance: An offscreen wgpu renderer draws a surface mesh with per-vertex and per-cell scalars, colour maps and a camera, writes PNG, and is compared with a CPU reference by pixel statistics. Limits are registered in ADR 0125.
note: Wave 47D (ADR 0125), wgpu 30.0.1. Size L. Registered check P2 (picking returns the scalar value) is an ignored known miss. Open decision: the egui front end (eframe 0.36.2) needs Rust 1.95 while the workspace builds on an older toolchain. Not done: cut planes, iso-surfaces, streamlines, particles, video.

title: Claude Code bridge library (rcfd-claude)
acceptance: The library lists Claude Code sessions for a project folder, tails a transcript, and sends a message to a closed session by resuming it in headless mode, with a conservative tool allow-list and no auto-approval. Behaviour was observed on one CLI build (2.1.310); a fixture set pins it.
note: Wave 47E (ADR 0126), fixes in ADR 0128 (allow-list refuses control files, fail-closed init check). Fixtures carry synthetic ids. Size M. Not done: a sidecar for approvals (only if the allow-list proves too narrow), tests against other CLI versions.

title: Studio application shell (egui on wgpu)
acceptance: A window opens a project folder and shows its cases and runs with state, scrubs a run through time with linked fields and residuals, edits case inputs with schema validation, and hosts the Claude Code chat sidebar. The checks listed in docs/ui-restart-plan.md section 6 each exist as a named test. A person views the result and reports.
note: Wave 48 in docs/ui-restart-plan.md. Starts only after the wave 47 results have been viewed. Size XL.

title: Claude Code plugin with project tools
acceptance: A Claude Code plugin ships an MCP server (extending rcfd-mcp) with tools to list projects and runs, edit project files with validation, start and stop runs, read metrics and compare runs; edits made from Claude Code show in the application. Protocol tests pass and one real session is checked where possible.
note: Wave 48 in docs/ui-restart-plan.md. Size L.

title: Design ledger and tolerance study driver
acceptance: Every design variant is recorded in a ledger with its inputs, solver version and results, and a tolerance study driver samples manufacturing spread and reports output spread against registered limits (ADR 0121).
note: Wave 46D (ADR 0121). Size M. Every model is a stated proxy until checked against measured fan data, which does not exist yet. Not done: uncertainty bands on the reduced-order model, automatic ledger logging from runs, Sobol sensitivity indices.

title: Test gate speed and strictness
acceptance: The full gate runs each test in its own process from a small pool with a per-test time limit, prints the summary format the older scripts read, and a scanner lists tests that cannot fail (ADRs 0127 to 0129, docs/test-process.md).
note: Size M. Open items: an environment switch that makes the 12 data-gated tests fail rather than skip; limit headroom on one stage; a test for the R3 limit; a re-measurement at 5 jobs; scanning of inline test modules; a slot queue in place of the directory locks. The T2 vacuous pass is closed by ADR 0235 C: t2b asserts the registered precondition over(BDF2) >= 0.02 (measured 2.467e-2, bounded 1.16e-9); the old T2 stays as an ignored setup_defect record.

title: Workspace layer (rcfd-workspace) shared by the MCP server and the Studio
acceptance: One crate holds the commands, queries and write rule for a project folder, and both the MCP project tools and the Studio use it: the existing project-tool and Studio tests pass unchanged, a Studio save and an edit_case on the same file give one write and one conflict naming the current hash, a comment line in a case survives a Studio save, and the crate graph stays acyclic with rcfd-studio not depending on rcfd-mcp (ADR 0173 W1, W2 and W5, checks C1, C2 and C6).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed 2026-11-04). Priority 1, set by the maintainer on 2026-11-04. Closes the race between Studio saves (save_if_base: no edit lock, no edits.jsonl entry) and edit_case. Size L. PARTIAL (ADR 0185, the registration of F-270, 2026-11-05, branch f270-workspace, not merged): the crate exists and the MCP project tools run on it (W1, W2); the Studio saves under the edit lock with a journal line, creates cases and starts runs through it (W5). Open: a comment line survives a Studio save only in the workspace's line-level form, which the Studio does not use, because the preview's save rule (ADR 0147, ADR 0148) and three Studio tests need the saved bytes to be the editor's whole text (ADR 0185 Q1, a maintainer question).

title: New simulations from the MCP server in project mode
acceptance: In project mode the MCP server creates a case in cases/ (from a shipped example, a built-in template, TOML, settings or a copy of a project case, never replacing a file) and starts a run of it through the runner, in one call if asked, with the same start plan as the Studio, so the run's fields are stored and the Studio lists the run and can read its snapshots (ADR 0173 R1, W3, check C7, decisions D7 and D2).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 2. The shared start plan changes start_run's output for cases with no store setting, so it needs the maintainer's approval (D7). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0186, the registration of F-271, 2026-11-05, branch f271-new-simulations, not merged): the project tool new_case makes cases/<name>.toml (or .json) from a shipped example, the built-in template, TOML, settings or a copy, validated first and never replacing a file; start_run makes a new case and runs it in one call with the Studio's field-store plan, so its fields are stored, and the Studio's run poller and store reader show it (C7). Open: start_run of an existing case applies the plan only with store: "plan", because the default change waits for the maintainer's approval of D7 (ADR 0186 Q2); the project tool is named new_case because the session tool create_case is the only way to make a session, so D2's hiding is left to F-275 (ADR 0186 Q1); the Studio still uses its own copy of the start plan, pinned equal by a parity test, until the maintainer's Studio work lands.

title: Mesh set-up from the MCP server in project mode
acceptance: In project mode the MCP server checks a case's mesh (the report of rcfd check-mesh and the patch list), draws it with the CPU renderer, imports a Gmsh, Fluent or OpenFOAM file from the project folder into meshes/ with its cell, face and patch counts, lists meshes/ with the cases that use each file, and returns the mesh check when edit_case changes a mesh setting; an invalid mesh setting is refused with a located diagnostic and writes nothing (ADR 0173 R2, W4, check C8, decision D8).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 3. Not included: a mesh recipe format and the surface-to-volume pipeline, which no case or command reaches today (D8 (b), a later ADR). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0187, the registration of F-272, 2026-11-05, branch f272-mesh-setup, not merged): the project tools check_case_mesh (the report of rcfd check-mesh and the patch list of a case's mesh), preview_mesh (a PNG coloured by a cell-quality measure, drawn by the CPU renderer), import_mesh (a Gmsh or Fluent file or an OpenFOAM folder read with the solver's readers, its cells, faces, patches, zones and bounds reported, copied into meshes/ without replacing anything) and list_meshes (meshes/ with the cases that use each mesh); edit_case builds and checks the edited mesh when a mesh setting changes and refuses, writing nothing, a mesh file outside the project (1004) or a mesh that cannot be built (1003, located); a case's mesh file is confined to the project folder by every mesh command (C8). Open: the check is named check_case_mesh because the session tool check_mesh holds the name until F-275 (ADR 0187 Q1); a mesh that builds but fails the quality check is written with mesh.ok false (Q2); no size limit on a mesh build (Q3); a preview over the size budget is drawn narrower (Q4); non-orthogonality is the default measure (Q5); the three new read tools are not in the Studio bridge's allow-list (Q6, the maintainer's); the public Fluent elbow is checked only where it is fetched. USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0187 decision record): the Studio's size limits, through a preview::estimate shared in the workspace, follow once the maintainer's Studio worktree has landed (Q3 (b), F-293); Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5 and Q6 were not asked (Q6 is (b) on main since F-275).

title: Project journal and change feed with who, what and why; the Studio updates from it
acceptance: Every accepted write, case creation, mesh import, run submission and run control call appends an entry to .rcfd/edits.jsonl with an actor, a sequence number, the settings changed (path, old and new value) and an optional reason (additive fields only); one ordered feed merges the journal, the run records and events, and the watcher's changes; a change made by one process appears in a second process's feed within the limit fixed by an amendment of ADR 0173, a write made outside the workspace appears as external, and the Studio updates its views from the feed and shows who changed what and why (ADR 0173 R3, W6, check C3, decision D4).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 4. Linking an MCP actor to a Claude Code session is NOT VERIFIED (ADR 0173 D4). Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0188, the registration of F-273, 2026-11-05, branch f273-journal-feed, not merged): every accepted write, case creation, mesh import, run submission and accepted run request of the workspace, from the MCP server and from the Studio, leaves one line in .rcfd/edits.jsonl with seq (given under a short project-wide lock), who, the actor {client, instance {pid, started}} (mcp, or studio for the Studio's saves and creations), the reason the caller gave and the changed settings with old and new values (additive fields and kinds only; lines written before still read); the feed (rcfd_workspace::feed, the MCP tool read_feed) merges the journal, the runs' state, warning and stop events and the watcher's changes, and labels a change no journal line explains external with its path only; an edit_case with a reason made by the rcfd-mcp binary reaches another process's feed at the first poll of 250 ms (limit 4), a plain write within 4 polls; the Studio's project worker reads the feed and says who changed what and why for changes another actor made (C3). Open: the Studio's run starts and controls are journaled without an actor until the maintainer's Studio worktree lands (ADR 0188 Q3); the run worker, a feed panel and a notes list in the Studio wait for that worktree (Q5); the feed is offered as the new tool read_feed, list_changes unchanged (Q1); a write_note line keeps kind edit (Q2); linking an mcp actor to a Claude Code session is NOT VERIFIED and not built (Q4); read_feed is not in the Studio bridge's allow-list (Q6, the maintainer's); a feed shows no history from before it was opened (Q7). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0188 decision record): the Studio's actor on its run starts and controls (Q3 (a)) and a feed panel and notes list (Q5 (a)) follow once the maintainer's Studio worktree has landed (F-293); no link from an mcp actor to a Claude Code session for now (Q4 (c)); Q1, Q2, Q6, Q7 and the run worker of Q5 were not asked.

title: Design study evaluations as runner runs in project mode
acceptance: In project mode each design evaluation is submitted to the runner as a run tagged with its study and variant (additive run-record fields), never more than max_runs at once; the metrics match the in-process evaluator for the same cases within the tolerance fixed by an amendment of ADR 0173, and the extra cost per evaluation is measured and recorded (ADR 0173 W7, check C4).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 5. Chained studies need the runner to start a run from a previous result; runner support for continue_from is not established. Size M. PARTIAL (ADR 0189, the registration of F-274, 2026-11-05, branch f274-design-evals, not merged): with --project, design_run_study and design_evaluate evaluate each candidate at each operating condition as one run of the project's runner, the base case with rcfd run --set entries checked to give the in-process settings tree, tagged in run.json with study, variant and condition (three optional fields, absent from every other run); the result is read from metrics.json by the in-process status rule; three points on the 32 x 32 cavity gave three tagged runs, at most max_runs = 2 at once, with records equal to the in-process ones bit for bit; one evaluation cost 0.64 s on the runner against 0.23 s in process (C4). Open: a chained study with several conditions, a study with its own max_steps and operating maps stay in the server process (the runner cannot start a run from another run's result or cap its steps; ADR 0189 Q2, Q3); runs that outlive a call are submitted again (Q5); no journal line for design runs and records yet (Q6, now that F-273 is merged); the design tools keep the access class write_files though they now start runs (Q7, F-275); the run-record fields need the lead's approval (Q4, ADR 0130). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0189 decision record): the run-record fields study, variant and condition are approved flat as built (Q4 (a), the lead's approval under ADR 0130); a runner setting to continue from a previous run, with a step cap, is the new item F-287 (Q2 (d), Q3 (d)); adopting matching runs is the new item F-288 (Q5 (b)); design_run_study and design_evaluate become access class execute, made separately (Q7); Q1, Q6 and Q8 were not asked.

title: Project-mode MCP tool list and plugin edit hook
acceptance: With --project, each session tool is hidden once its project equivalent has passed its check, until tools/list holds no tool whose state lives only in the server's memory; without --project it is byte-identical to before; the plugin refuses Claude Code's own Edit and Write under cases/, runs/ and designs/ with a message naming edit_case and create_case, checked in a real session where possible (ADR 0173 W8, check C5, decisions D2 and D5).
note: ADR 0173 (proposed). Priority 6. The hook contract is to be checked on an installed Claude Code build first. Size S. PARTIAL (ADR 0195, the registration of F-275, 2026-11-06, branch f275-project-mode-tools, not merged): with --project the 16 session tools whose every use needs or makes a session (create_case, set_setting, get_setting, load_mesh, check_mesh, run, status, get_residuals, get_field_stats, export_vtk, the four workflow tools, run_headless, render_image) are neither listed nor callable, 40 tools remain, the 17 kept session tools byte-identical; without --project tools/list and initialize are byte-identical; read_feed gains from_seq, which replays the journal (ADR 0188 Q7 (b)); the Studio bridge's first allow-list gains read_feed, check_case_mesh, preview_mesh and list_meshes (ADR 0187 Q6 (b), ADR 0188 Q6 (b)); the plugin's PreToolUse hook (rcfd-mcp --edit-hook) refuses Edit, Write, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit under cases/, runs/ and designs/ of an rcfd project, checked in a real Claude Code 2.1.319 session (C5-R). Open: the message names edit_case and new_case, not create_case, since new_case and check_case_mesh keep their names (Q1); the workflow tools and run_headless's restart, interpolation and checkpoint options have no project equivalent and are not offered (Q2); access classes unchanged (Q6); the hook under bypassPermissions is NOT VERIFIED; existing allow-list files are not changed (Q4); with 15 first rules, a rule the user adds is below the fold of the Studio's confirmation dialog until scrolled (Q8, amendment 1). USER DECISION 2026-11-06 (ADR 0195 decision record): design_run_study and design_evaluate become access class execute, made separately (Q6 (a) overturned); the hook's gaps are accepted: it fails open (Q7 (a)), shell writes are not guarded (Q5 (a)), and the bypass modes stay untested; the run-record fields of F-274 are approved (item 8); the other items of Decisions needed were not asked.

title: Particle splash and rebound at a wall film (impact regime maps)
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. Parcels that reach the wall film of F-253 are absorbed, rebound or splash by an impact regime map taken from a published source that the ADR names and reads (constants read from the source): for parcel streams set in each regime the model gives the regime and the rebound or splash outcome of the source's relations, and the parcel mass ledger of F-253 (injected = airborne + deposited + escaped + stuck + film + drained) balances with the new outcomes counted, each within limits fixed by its registration ADR; runs without the new setting are unchanged bit for bit (the records R1 to R4 of ADRs 0192 and 0194 and the baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0192 Q4 and ADR 0194 Q5: a new item, not part of F-254 (ADR 0192 recommended F-254, ADR 0194 a new item). It needs its own sources (impact regime maps) and checks; none has been read yet. ADR 0192's list of what it does not deliver also names breakup at impact; whether breakup belongs here is for the registration ADR.

title: Default steady kernel diverging on F-208's warped mesh W from n = 32: diagnose and fix
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. Registered diagnosis runs locate the growing mode by which the default steady simple/simplec kernel diverges on F-208's warped mesh W from n = 32 (ADR 0193 amendment 1: growth of about 1.8 times per iteration under every relaxation, viscosity, convection scheme, corrector count, pseudo-time, face_flux and SIMPLEC set-up tried; the pressure-velocity step from HbyA to the corrected velocity is suspected, not proven), and a fix makes the kernel converge on W at n = 32 and 64 under F-246's registered set-up, within limits fixed by its registration ADR, with the defaults bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged) unless the maintainer lifts that rule for the fix. Afterwards F-246's missed M1 check on W (the ignored tests m1_w_v1_known_miss and m1_w_v2_known_miss) is run again with its registered set-up and limits unchanged; how the fix is switched on for that run is fixed by the registration ADR.
note: From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0193 Q9: option (b), as recommended (the evidence points at the pressure-velocity step, not at the face gradient), not (c), reopening the dropped warped-face item. W stays the binding warped mesh of F-246 and W2 is supplementary evidence only (ADR 0193 Q8 (a)). ADR 0193 amendment 1 found the divergence to be a property of the default kernel on W, not of the harness. RESULT (ADR 0198, branch f285-warped-kernel, not merged): the deferred non-orthogonal correction of the pressure equation diverges on W from n = 32 (its step has an eigenvalue of about -1.18; 0.86 at n = 16); the opt-in library field SimpleSolver::implicit_non_orth_pressure solves that part implicitly (GMRES) and, with face_flux, the kernel converges on W at n = 16, 32 and 64 (218, 716, 2489 iterations), converged results elsewhere unchanged to 3e-12; F-246's M1 on W run again with it is met (skew_corrected 1.994 / 1.780, body_force_weighted 1.990 / 1.662, limits 1.7 / 1.2); defaults unchanged; the status is left to the maintainer (ADR 0198 Q1 to Q5).

title: Transient k-omega SST with pimple on a static mesh
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. turbulence.model = k_omega_sst runs with the pimple algorithm on a static mesh, which the case tree refuses today with a located error at turbulence.model (ADR 0183 PC-5): the k and omega equations get their time derivative and are updated within the outer iterations (ADR 0183 amendment P-C, question 8 (a)), also with a rotating_frame source, so that check H of ADR 0183 can run as registered; the transient terms are checked against closed forms named in the ADR, within limits fixed by its registration ADR; steady SST runs and every existing transient run are unchanged bit for bit (baseline hashes unchanged).
note: Prerequisite of EXP-ROT check H (ADR 0183; the experiment's roadmap item F-276 is on the unmerged branch m0-gate-roadmap). From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to question 8 of ADR 0183 amendment P-C: transient SST is its own item, and check H stays NOT RUNNABLE until it lands. k-omega SST on moving meshes is another item (F-277 on the same branch). ADR 0136 lists URANS as missing. BUILT (ADR 0199, the registration of F-286, 2026-11-06, branch f286-transient-sst, not merged): k_omega_sst runs with pimple on a static mesh, one sweep with the time derivative of solver.time_scheme at the start of every outer iteration (piso, k-epsilon and SA without DES stay refused); the decay recursions and closed forms, the k budget, the steady state against SIMPLEC (1.7e-9) and the rotating frame meet their limits, defaults bit-identical; the case-tree BDF2 order check is a known miss (p 2.4 to 2.7, pre-asymptotic); check H's case text builds and its smoke is finite.

title: Runner run setting: continue from a previous run (rcfd run --continue-from), with a step cap
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. A run setting that the runner passes to rcfd run --continue-from (a change to RunSettings and the launch; ADR 0189 Q2 (d)) and a run setting for the step cap (ADR 0189 Q3 (d)), so that in project mode a chained design study with several conditions, a study with its own max_steps and an operating map (design_run_operating_map) are evaluated on the runner instead of in the server process; their records match the in-process evaluator for the same cases within the tolerance fixed by its registration ADR, and a run without the new settings keeps the bytes of its run.json and its results.
note: From the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0189 Q2 and Q3: option (d) of each, as recommended; until this lands such studies stay in the server process (option (a), as built). Operating maps move with it (ADR 0189 Q2). It is also the project-mode equivalent of run_headless's continue_from that ADR 0195 Q2 names. A new run-record field needs the lead's approval (ADR 0130). PARTIAL (ADR 0200, the registration of F-287, 2026-11-06, branch f287-f288-runner, not merged): run.json settings gains continue_from (a run id) and max_steps, each written only when set (rcfd_runner::records::LaunchSettings, read beside RunSettings so that the Studio's struct literal is unchanged); the runner passes rcfd run --continue-from runs/<id>/output/restart.rcfd and the new rcfd run --max-steps (the drive's step cap); with --project a chained study, a study with its own max_steps and design_run_operating_map run on the runner, a chained condition or map point continuing from the run before when its restart file fits; a run continued after 25 steps ends where a run of 50 steps does, bit for bit (R-1c); on the 16 x 16 cavity the continued conditions and map points agree with the in-process chain to 5.6e-10 and 6.7e-10 relative on lid_drag (limit 1e-4), the cold and step-capped runs bit for bit (C-CH, C-MS, C-MAP); design_run_operating_map has the class execute with --project. Open: the two settings need the lead's approval (ADR 0130, ADR 0200 Q1); ADR 0200 Q2 to Q7 (a source run that has not ended, what continue_from names, tags of map runs, the class of design_run_operating_map, the iteration cap of a continued run, a condition with another mesh of the same size).

title: Adopt matching runs when a restarted MCP server resumes a design study
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. In project mode, before a design-study candidate is submitted, the server adopts a run of the project's runner with the same tags (study, variant, condition), case snapshot hash and entries, waiting for it or reading its metrics.json (ADR 0189 Q5 (b)); after the MCP server is stopped during a study and started again, the next call submits no second run for a candidate that has one, and the adopted records equal those of a study that was not interrupted, within limits fixed by its registration ADR; a candidate without a matching run is submitted as before.
note: From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0189 Q5: option (b), as recommended. Until this lands, runs that outlive a call are submitted again (option (a), as built). PARTIAL (ADR 0201, the registration of F-288, 2026-11-06, branch f287-f288-runner, not merged): before a study's run is submitted, a run of the project with the same tags, case, case bytes, entries, launch settings and solver version that has not failed or been cancelled is adopted, waited for or read from its metrics.json, and the result gains runs_adopted; an rcfd-mcp killed during a three-point study and started again made no new run and adopted the three, its records bit for bit those of an uninterrupted study, and a chained study killed after two of its runs ended with exactly one run per variant and condition (A-R); ten decoys that differ in one item of the key, or failed or were cancelled, were not adopted (A-N). Open: ADR 0201 Q1 to Q5 (the solver version in the key, failed runs, operating maps, the index, runs of an earlier definition).

title: Conjugate heat_flow report with the gradient options, checked by a heat balance
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. The conjugate heat_flow report (conductive_face_flows) uses the gradient options of F-256 that the energy equation was solved with (ADR 0190 Q3 (b)); on a skewed conjugate case with gradient_boundary = corrected or dropped, the face correction or a limiter set, the reported flows balance against the source to the solver tolerance, within a limit fixed by its registration ADR; without the options the report is unchanged bit for bit (baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0190 Q3: option (b) as its own item with a balance check, as recommended. Until this lands, with the options set the report adds the default operator's non-orthogonal terms, so on skewed cells it is not the flux the matrix solved (option (a), documented). DONE (ADR 0202, 2026-11-06, branch f289-f290, not merged): rcfd_fv::cht::conductive_face_flows_opt applies the solver's limiter, face correction and boundary treatment to the face flows, and the conjugate heat_flow report passes the energy solver's options (no key, no rule); on the skewed conjugate case of ADR 0202 (wedge mesh of 29.6 degrees, a solid zone with a source of 2.67e-2 W) the reports balance the source to the solver residual for the default and the seven option sets (imbalance 3.2e-13 to 3.3e-13 W, limit tol_W + 1e-12 F, about 2e-12 W), per material too, and the face flows are the solved operator per cell (at most 4.5e-16, and 7.1e-15 on a 3-D skewed two-material mesh, limit 1e-12), while the unchanged formula misses the balance by 2.0e-6 to 2.1e-3 W; without the options the report is unchanged bit for bit; baseline hashes and H1 unedited. Open: the heat_flow report of a case without solid zones has no secondary flux (ADR 0202 Q1).

title: Inverse-volume mesh smoothing in the case tree
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. A third value inverse_volume of dynamic_mesh.smoothing.method, with its exponent from dynamic_mesh.smoothing.exponent (an enumeration value, no new key; ADR 0191 Q2 (b)), runs the InverseVolume(k) displacement-diffusion stiffness of ADR 0090 D4, today in the library only: invalid settings give located errors, a tree run equals the library run to a limit fixed by its registration ADR, and a case without the value is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0191 Q2: option (b), a separate small item, as recommended. DONE (ADR 0203, 2026-11-06, branch f289-f290, not merged): dynamic_mesh.smoothing.method = inverse_volume runs ADR 0090 D4's InverseVolume(k) stiffness with k = smoothing.exponent on the incompressible and the compressible moving paths (no key, no new rule; the stiffness uses the initial volumes, as the displacement is solved from the initial mesh); the tree gives the library's points bit for bit at every step of ADR 0033's piston on a mesh graded 8 (exponents 1 and 2) and the library run's state bit for bit on ADR 0191's compressible piston (314 steps), and exponent 0 equals laplacian bit for bit; on the piston, against laplacian at every step, the smallest cell is never smaller (0.945 against 0.75 of its initial volume at the end) and the largest volume ratio and aspect ratio are never larger (aspect 7.39 against 9.32); invalid settings give located errors; cases without the value keep their settings hashes (five recorded before the change) and their bits; baseline hashes and H1 unedited. Open: whether an inverse method outside smoothing should be refused (ADR 0203 Q1).

title: Gradient options on turbulence transport, momentum, pressure and the electric potential
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. The gradient options of F-256 (face correction, secondary limiter, boundary-gradient treatment) also act on the turbulence transport equations, momentum, the pressure equation and the electric potential, each under new checks of the kinds F-256 used (ADR 0190 G1 to G4): invalid values give located errors, a tree run equals the library run with the same options to a limit fixed by its registration ADR, the options change the result on a non-orthogonal mesh, and a case without the keys is bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From the maintainer's answer of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0190 Q4: option (b), a new item with new checks (the recommendation was (a)). ADR 0016 D2 defined and checked the options on the scalar sweep only. DONE (ADR 0204, 2026-11-06, branch f291-gradient-options, not merged): an optional table [solver.gradient_equations] with the booleans momentum, pressure, turbulence and electric_potential (absent from the data and the settings hash unless set) makes those equations take the F-256 options too: the momentum Laplacian and the pressure equation (with the internal faces of its flux correction and the SIMPLEC non-orthogonal compensation) of the steady and transient constant-density kernels, the k-epsilon, SST and Spalart-Allmaras transports, and the potential of electric.enabled; the energy and scalar terms take them as before. Invalid values and selectors that would act on nothing are located errors (R1, R5 to R8, each with a control; G1). On the 29.6-degree wedge mesh every tree run equals its library run bit for bit (limit 1e-12 of each field's scale) for momentum (steady, seven sets; transient, C2), pressure (steady, seven sets; with the SIMPLEC compensation and transient, C2), SST (seven sets), k-epsilon and SA (C2) and the electric potential (seven sets), and every set moves the result by 6.4e-6 to 23 of the scale (limit 1e-9); on a 38-degree skewed box the flux correction with the options carries the pressure operator's face flux per cell to 1.5e-15 of the flux scale, which the unchanged flux correction misses by 4.4e-3 to 0.26. Without the table every result and settings hash is unchanged, a new case writes no table; baseline hashes and H1 unedited. Amendments 1 and 2: the k-epsilon and SA cases were registered with the moving lid as a wall, which those models refuse (records kept, corrected cases T2b and T3b); P1's default run diverges (SIMPLEC with a corrector, no compensation), P2-all is supplementary evidence. Open: the names (ADR 0204 Q1), the electric current and Joule heat with the options (Q2), the flux correction on fixed-pressure faces (Q3: the default misses its operator there by 2.9e-2 of the flux scale with correctors, dropped closes it), the pressure-lag estimate (Q4), the Lorentz potential (Q5), body_force_weighted (Q6), other solvers and models (Q7), the P1 set-up (Q8).

title: Gas buoyancy and gas shear in the particle wall film
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. Two opt-in additions to the film of F-253: gas buoyancy, the film driven by (rho_l - rho_g) g_t in place of rho_l g_t (ADR 0192 Q2 (b)), and gas shear, a shear-driven closure checked against h = (2 mu_l Gamma / (rho_l tau_g))^(1/2) for a film driven by shear alone (ADR 0192 Q3 (a)); each meets a closed form derived in the ADR within limits fixed by its registration ADR, the parcel mass ledger of F-253 balances, and runs without them are unchanged bit for bit (F-253's checks, the records R1 and R2 and the baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-06 to ADR 0192 Q2 and Q3, both added as an item (ADR 0192 recommended leaving them out until a case needs them). The film of F-253 stays without them. PARTIAL (ADR 0206, the registration of F-292, 2026-11-06, branch f292-film-gas, not merged): every registered check is met; marking the item done is the maintainer's (ADR 0206 Q1). Opt-in keys particles.film.gas_buoyancy and gas_shear (hash_omit_default; library FilmGas, Tracker::set_film_gas): the buoyant film under a gas of 250 kg/m^3 is within 3.3e-15 of h_B as a window average, the shear-driven film under 0.1 Pa within 2.7e-14 of (2 mu_l Gamma/(rho_l tau))^(1/2), the ledger closes to 1.8e-12, the tree equals the library bit for bit, seven mutations made their checks fail, and runs without the keys are unchanged bit for bit (R1 to R7, baseline hashes, H1). Open: ADR 0206 Q2 to Q6.

title: Studio follow-ups that wait on the maintainer's Studio worktree
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR, written before any code and after the maintainer's worktree studio-case-lineage has landed on main: (1) the Studio's run starts and controls are journaled with the Studio's actor, one with_actor at each of the four RunService constructions (ADR 0188 Q3 (a)); (2) a Studio panel lists the change feed with who, what and why, and a notes/ list (ADR 0188 Q5 (a)); (3) box_3d is in the Studio's and the workspace start plan's generator lists, with a cell estimate (ADR 0191 Q4 (a)); (4) the MCP server's mesh builds use the Studio's size limits (2 000 000 estimated cells, 256 MiB) through one preview::estimate moved from the Studio into the workspace layer, which the Studio's preview also uses (ADR 0187 Q3 (b)). Each part has named tests, and the existing Studio and project-tool tests pass.
note: From the maintainer's answers of 2026-11-06: the maintainer lands studio-case-lineage first, and these follow (ADR 0187 Q3, ADR 0188 Q3 and Q5, ADR 0191 Q4). Agents do not touch that worktree. The third change ADR 0188 Q5 names, the run worker reading the feed in place of its own poll, was not part of the answer and stays an open question of ADR 0188.

title: Transient k-epsilon and Spalart-Allmaras (without DES) on pimple
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. k-epsilon and Spalart-Allmaras without DES run with the pimple algorithm on a static mesh, which the case tree refuses today; each model gets its own registration with its time derivative (the existing k-epsilon kernel has none, and the Spalart-Allmaras one is once per step and Euler only), checked against closed forms named in the ADR; steady runs and every existing transient run are unchanged bit for bit.
note: From ADR 0199 (F-286) question 2, recommendation taken by the lead: a follow-up item, each model with its own registration. SA-DES and the Reynolds stress model stay on their once-per-step path (ADR 0199 question 3), because moving them would change existing transient results. PARTIAL (ADR 0210, the registration of F-294, 2026-11-07, branch f294-transient-keps-sa, not merged): every registered check is met except one, a known miss. k_epsilon (every variant, wall function and wall treatment) and spalart_allmaras with des = off run with pimple on a static mesh, one sweep with the time derivative of solver.time_scheme at the start of every outer iteration (the F-286 path, chosen by the model); piso stays refused, SA-DES and SA-DDES keep their once-per-step Euler path. The decay recursions meet to 6.1e-15 and the closed forms give the orders of the schemes, the k and nuTilda budgets close to 1e-15, the steady states equal SIMPLEC (1.6e-9, 5.4e-10), the rotating frame runs, and the case-tree time order meets for SA (BDF2 1.93, 2.20) and for k-epsilon with Euler; k-epsilon with BDF2 is a known miss (p 0.80 to 1.53, rising to 1.81 to 1.89 two levels finer). Defaults bit-identical. Open: ADR 0210 Q1 to Q7.

title: One diffusivity per periodic seam pair
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. On a periodic seam each face of a pair takes one common diffusivity, so that k, omega and momentum diffusion is conservative across a seam where the eddy viscosity differs; the option is opt-in with defaults bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged), and a global budget on a periodic case with a differing eddy viscosity is checked within a limit fixed by the ADR.
note: From ADR 0199 (F-286) amendment 2 and question 5, recommendation taken by the lead: found while correcting the F-286 set-ups; each face of a seam pair takes the diffusivity of its own owner cell. FAN-01 and EXP-ROT check H both have rotational seams, so this item comes before check H is read.

title: One diffusivity per periodic seam pair for the other models
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. The rule of F-295 (turbulence.periodic_seam.diffusivity = "pair") is applied to the face viscosity or diffusivity of k-epsilon, Spalart-Allmaras, the Reynolds stress model, the subgrid and mixing-length models and the rheology face viscosity, each with a global-budget check on a periodic box with a differing viscosity (the owner rule must miss it, the pair rule must meet it); defaults bit-identical (baseline hashes unchanged).
note: From ADR 0205 (F-295) question 1, recommendation taken by the lead: a low-priority follow-up with checks of the same kind. Question 2: EXP-ROT check H and FAN-01 do not set the key yet; the EXP-ROT job amends ADR 0183 to set pair before H runs. Question 3: the default stays owner. BUILT (ADR 0212, the registration of F-296, 2026-11-07, branch f296-pair-diffusivity, not merged): every registered check is met. turbulence.periodic_seam.diffusivity = "pair" now also gives both faces of a periodic pair one value (the model's internal-face formula across the seam) for k-epsilon (momentum, k and epsilon), Spalart-Allmaras (momentum, nuTilda), the Reynolds stress model (momentum, its momentum-source viscosity, stresses and epsilon), smagorinsky, wale and mixing_length (momentum) and a laminar run's viscosity law (rheology); refused with laminar without a law and with plugin. The global diffusion budgets close to 1e-15 with pair and miss by 4.9e-3 to 3.2e-2 with owner; the one-sweep k, nuTilda, stress and epsilon budgets (seam lag accounted) close to 5e-15 with pair and miss by 1.4e-4 to 5.7e-2 with owner; the case-tree seam pairs are equal to the bit. Finding: SA's nuTilda diffusivity is already one value per pair under owner. ADR 0205 S1 is an ignored record (superseded). Defaults bit-identical. Open: ADR 0212 Q1 to Q5.

title: NSGA-II per-variable crossover and the 30-parameter ZDT1 check
acceptance: A new registration ADR re-registers MO1z (ZDT1 with 30 parameters, C within its limit) with the per-variable coordinate exchange between parents added to NSGA-II (ADR 0209 diagnostic DG1: C about 1.5e-3 with it), after the operator is read from Deb 2002 and the crossover and mutation papers; the MO1z known miss is then met or recorded again with its numbers; defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0209 (F-249) question 5, recommendation taken by the lead. F-249 stays partial for the MO1z and N3 known misses (N3: the Nelder-Mead start rule gives a tiny step near zero; question 3 keeps MATLAB's rule). Open for the maintainer: questions 1 (done or partial), 6 (tool description naming nsga2 needs a registered golden edit) and 7 (extended warm start as default needs the bit-identity lift). BUILT (ADR 0220, the registration of F-297, 2026-11-07, branch f297-nsga2-crossover, not merged): every registered check is met. The opt-in crossover = "exchange" of nsga2 (library nsga2::run_with, Method::Nsga2With, the design tools' method.crossover) exchanges the two children's values of each variable of a crossed pair with probability 1/2. ZDT1 with 30 parameters (25 000 evaluations, population 100): C 1.5e-3, 1.3e-3, 1.6e-3 on seeds 1 to 3 (limit 1e-2; G and I met), the numbers of DG1; FON within the limits (C at most 5.9e-3). The default sbx is bit-identical (V0b record) and still misses ZDT1 (C 0.543; the ADR 0209 known miss stays ignored). Read: Deb et al. (2002), Deb and Agrawal (1995, 1999), Deb and Deb (2012); Deb and Goyal (1996) not obtained. The papers cross each variable with probability 0.5 and state no exchange (recorded diagnostics DP1, DP2). Open: ADR 0220 Q1 to Q5 (the reading clause, the papers' rule, the default, bounded forms, the tool description).

title: Electric current and Joule heat with the gradient options, and the fixed-pressure flux correction
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. (a) When electric_potential takes the gradient options (F-291), the current density and the Joule heat use the same face flows, with a current balance check (the F-289 pattern; the default must miss it, the option must meet it). (b) First measure what the 2.9e-2 mismatch of the default flux correction beside skewed fixed-pressure faces (ADR 0204 question 3) does to the mass balance of a converged run; only if it matters, give the flux correction the equation's boundary term under the options. Defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0204 (F-291) questions 2 and 3, recommendations (b) and (c) taken by the lead. Questions 1, 4 to 8: recommendation (a) taken (optional table kept; PISO/PIMPLE lag estimate on the default operator; Lorentz-source potential not wired; body_force_weighted refused with pressure options; other solvers and models refused; P1 binding with P2-all supplementary). DONE (ADR 0221, 2026-11-07, branch f298-joule-heat, not merged). (a) With solver.gradient_equations.electric_potential the boundary current density and the Joule heat use the currents of the operator the potential was solved with (rcfd-fv electric::face_currents_opt, joule_heat_opt, boundary_power_opt; a cell's Joule heat is half the face power F_f (phi_o - phi_n) of its internal faces plus F_b (phi_P - phi_b) of its boundary faces, so the total is the boundary power up to the solver's residual). On the 29.6-degree wedge, for the seven option sets, the boundary currents add up to zero within the solver tolerance (at most 2.2e-16 A against bounds of 2.2e-12 A), per group of cells too, and the Joule heat equals the electric power to 5e-16 W (P 0.24 to 0.27 W); the tree's current density and heat are the library's. The unchanged currents miss the domain balance by 4.7e-7 to 1.9e-3 A (every set that changes boundary faces) and a group balance for every set; the unchanged Joule heat misses the power by 3.0e-2 to 3.6e-2 W; the default's own Joule heat misses its power by 3.1e-2 W (11.9 percent) on the skewed mesh (kept, ADR 0221 Q1). (b) Measured first: in a converged SIMPLE channel on the wedge with a fixed-pressure outlet and one corrector the default flux correction leaves a domain mass imbalance of 2.0e-3 of the inflow and 6.8e-4 in one outlet cell (interior 3e-14; 5.0e-3 with SIMPLEC and its compensation; with gradient_boundary dropped 2e-13), which matters by the registered rule (1e-6). So under the pressure options (solver.gradient_equations.pressure) the flux correction now takes the equation's non-orthogonal part on fixed-pressure faces (owner, corrected or none): on the 38-degree box it carries the operator's flux to 7.3e-16 of the cell scale on the outlet cells (6.6e-2 to 2.6e-1 without), and the converged channel runs close their mass balance (at most 1.3e-12 of the inflow) for six sets. Defaults bit-identical (the default and dropped runs' hashes, the settings hash and every field of the electric case unchanged; baseline hashes and H1 unedited). Amendment 2: Some(GradientOptions::default()) is None in the new functions (found by ADR 0204 G4 (iv)). Open: the default Joule heat on skewed meshes (Q1), the default flux correction on fixed-pressure faces (Q2), a negative cell Joule heat under the options (Q3, none seen), the SIMPLEC boundary compensation under the options (Q4).

title: PISO/PIMPLE instability at large cell diffusion number across a thin gap
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. The mechanism of the failure found in ADR 0211 amendment 1 is identified (fixed mesh, block at rest, time step above between tau/40 and tau/20, cell diffusion number 3 to 6 across the gap; not removed by dropping the Rhie-Chow time term, IC0 pressure solver, upwind convection, 3 correctors, 5 PIMPLE outer iterations or cell aspect ratios 16 and 8), and either removed with the ignored tau/10 known-miss test of F-244 then passing, or recorded as a located limit with a refusal; defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0211 (F-244) question 4, recommendation taken by the lead. Questions 1 to 3: recommendation taken (the 2026-10-22 decision approves the refined acceptance text; no case-tree version, T4 covers the tree path; F-244 done). PARTIAL (ADR 0214, 2026-11-07): mechanism located (H-RC: the first corrector over-corrects a pressure error by about the cross-gap diffusion number, and on the collocated mesh the second corrector leaves the Rhie-Chow part of a pressure wave of four cells along the gap; twin-run radii within 0.6 % of the replica); removed under the library opt-in PimpleSettings::consistent_correctors (SIMPLEC-type correctors, defaults bit-identical), with which the registered tau/10 set-up of F-244 passes (A1c: U(10 tau)/U_t 1.00548). Open: the default path (the known miss of F-244 still fails by construction; ADR 0214 Q1), a refusal on the moving-mesh default path (Q3), a case key (Q4).

title: Transient RANS follow-ups from F-294
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code.
