(a) `rcfd_turb::supports_transient` says which models run transient on pimple (k-epsilon, SA without DES, SST), checked by a test against what the case tree accepts; (b) an amendment to ADR 0199 re-registers S3 for SST from the wall-matching start that F-294 used (BDF2 order in the band in the probe), the old S3 kept as an ignored record; (c) k-epsilon BDF2 order (known miss of ADR 0210, p = 0.80 / 1.49 / 1.53): test the suspected cause, the kink of the wall-function eddy viscosity at y* = 11.53, with a smooth variant under a registered check; defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0210 (F-294) questions 3, 5 and 7, recommendations taken by the lead. Questions 1, 2, 4 and 6: keep piso refused, one ADR with two parts, plugin models refused on pimple, the enhanced wall function accepted and documented for wall-resolved meshes.

title: PISO consistent correctors: moving-mesh lag estimate, case key and benchmarks
acceptance: Every limit is fixed by its registration ADR before any code. (a) The lag estimate of ADR 0073 is defined on a moving mesh per step, with the pre-run warning and adaptive correctors connected to it (ADR 0214 question 3); (b) a case key (for example `solver.consistent_correctors`) with the schema golden edit registered, and the LagCheck documentation and Raise message corrected, since a second corrector does not remove the lag for short waves on thin cells (questions 4 and 7); (c) a registered benchmark set (the ADR 0069 and 0073 harnesses, the ADR 0154 cylinder K1 and K2, the Studio examples) run with the option, and only then a decision on the default (question 1: the default stays false until then); defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0214 (F-299) questions 1 and 3 to 7, recommendations taken by the lead; question 2: F-299 stays partial. Question 5: extend the refused combinations one at a time, each with a steady-state identity check. PARTIAL (ADR 0223, 2026-11-08). Delivered: (a) at library level, PimpleSettings::moving_mesh_lag (default false): the ADR 0073 estimate, the run-time check and the adaptive corrector count on a moving-mesh step, on that step's own matrices, and PimpleSolver::lag_preflight_moving (the pre-run estimate of the next moving step); on the falling block of F-244 the moving step's estimate is within 4.3 % of its own twin-run radius (3.29 against 3.16; 0.917 against 0.920 with the consistent correctors), the adaptive count picks 8 correctors and passes A1 (1.00547). (b) The optional case table [solver.consistent_correctors] enabled (hash_omit_default; no golden or existing test changed, K0), bit-identical to the library option, with located errors; the consistent correctors extended to periodic faces and body forces (consistent_periodic, consistent_body_force, each with a steady identity check); the LagCheck documentation and the Raise message corrected. (c) The benchmark set run with the option: ADR 0069's order and cavity harnesses, ADR 0073's B2 and B3, ADR 0154's K1 and K2, ADR 0069's BDF2 cylinder, the Studio cylinder examples: every run stable with the option (the cavity's 88 required and 56 scan runs, the B2 box, K1 and K2 clean with M_hf 5.7e-3), the examples' St and cd within 0.6 %, the temporal orders unchanged; known misses of the option: DC4 (the MMS pressure error 1.119 x the default's at dt 0.025) and DC5 (TG PISO coarse order 2.305, band top 2.3). Defaults bit-identical (N2). Missing (why partial): the case-level wiring of the moving-mesh estimate (SV301 and the adaptive count for dynamic meshes; ADR 0156's refusal test A9b would change, Q2) and the periodic pressure identity S1p3 (known miss: 2.49e-10 of the range against 1e-10, below the default's own drift). Open: the default (Q1, recommended false until the remaining refused combinations are extended), one flag (Q3), the remaining refusals (Q5).

title: Periodic seam pair diffusivity: remaining viscosities and the pimple check
acceptance: Pair diffusivity covers the temperature-dependent properties viscosity and the user-function viscosity; a case-tree check of k-epsilon and Spalart-Allmaras with pair on pimple.
note: From ADR 0212 questions 1 and 4, taken at the recommendation. RSM on a rotational seam only if RSM ever runs there. The lead ignored f294_transient_keps_sa S1 after the F-296 merge (it asserted that pair is refused with k-epsilon); its other accept and refuse cases are no longer run and are to be restored in the pimple check.

title: Sliding interface in the case tree: rotor-stator generator, simulation loop and a non-axisymmetric check
acceptance: A case file runs a sliding rotor-stator interface from the CLI; an optional table or hash_omit_default keys carry it; a registered non-axisymmetric flow check sees the rotor mesh flux (ADR 0216 question 7).
note: From ADR 0216 questions 1 and 7, recommendations taken. Golden edits, if any, are listed for the maintainer.

title: Planar and sector sliding interfaces
acceptance: A planar sliding interface and a periodic sector join conserve mass and a uniform flow to round-off; periodic pairs are kept by the join.
note: From ADR 0216 question 3, recommendation taken: a separate item.

title: Local remeshing in the case tree (compressible solver)
acceptance: dynamic_mesh.deformation = remeshing runs a compressible case from the CLI; the tetrahedral generator and h0 in an optional table so existing case hashes are unchanged.
note: From ADR 0215 question 1, recommendation taken.

title: Tetrahedral mesher panic on a thin box (tetmesh neighbour link)
acceptance: tetrahedralize of box_surface([0,0,0],[1,0.1,0.1],[10,1,1]) at size 0.035 and quality_sweeps 3 returns a mesh or a located error instead of panicking at tetmesh.rs:386.
note: Found during F-247 (ADR 0215 question 7); recommendation taken: a new item. DONE (ADR 0228, the registration of F-306, 2026-11-08, branch f306-tetmesh-thin-box, merged 2026-11-09): every registered check is met; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0228 Q1). Cause: try_edge_removal accepted a ring triangle whenever the edge's two ends lay on opposite sides of it, so a triangle folded across a reflex corner of the ring passed; its new cells overlapped the cells outside the ring, and a later replace read the broken neighbour link. The same defect returned Ok with overlapping cells for neighbouring inputs, also with default options (a plate panics with default options; an STL candidate of ADR 0107 overlaps). Fix: a ring triangle is accepted only in the ring's turning sense (od == -s, oe == s, with the ring's sign checked on every ring edge), as F-247's remesher already does; no option, no new field. The acceptance input returns a valid mesh (1427 cells: every cell positive, volume equal to the enclosed volume to 1e-12, to_mesh Ok); so do the twelve other inputs of the registered sweep that fold on main and the STL input. The 118 fold-free inputs (111 boxes and closed shapes, 7 STL candidates) are bit-identical to fingerprints recorded on main (Windows); the existing suites pass. Three mutations failed their checks. Three opt-in quality-pass outputs that were valid on main after a fold (size 0.0333, sweeps 1 to 3) change. Open: ADR 0228 Q1 (acceptance), Q2 (the invariant expects), Q3 (an output validity check inside tetrahedralize, recommended as a follow-up), Q4 (unconditional fix), Q5, Q6 (Linux records).

title: Immersed solids in the case tree: optional immersed_solids table
acceptance: A case file with an optional immersed_solids table runs the F-219 forcing from the CLI; the penalty warns below 1e3 times the largest fluid diagonal; the schema golden edit is registered and approved by the maintainer.
note: From ADR 0218 questions 2 and 3, recommendations taken. Needs the maintainer's approval of the schema golden edit before it merges.

title: Moving immersed shapes
acceptance: An oscillating cylinder gives the force and the wake against a body-fitted moving-mesh run within a registered limit.
note: From ADR 0218 question 4, recommendation taken.

title: Second-order immersed forcing: fluid-solid face flux at the surface crossing
acceptance: Circular Couette flow with an immersed rotating cylinder reaches an observed order of 1.5 (the F-219 V1 check, limit unchanged).
note: From ADR 0218 question 6, recommendation taken. F-219's V1 order was 1.02, an ignored known-miss test.

title: NSGA-II: exchange crossover as the default for new studies, and the tool description
acceptance: create_study writes crossover = exchange into new nsga2 studies while old studies keep sbx; the design_create_study description names nsga2 and crossover; both goldens updated by a registered edit.
note: From ADR 0220 questions 3 and 5. Changes the tools' default output, so it needs the bit-identity lift and the golden edit approved by the maintainer; not started.

title: Default Joule heat and fixed-pressure flux correction: lift the bit-identity rule
acceptance: The default Joule heat equals the electric power on skewed meshes (it misses by 11.9 percent on the F-298 wedge) and the default flux correction on fixed-pressure faces closes the domain mass balance (it leaves 2.0e-3 of the inflow); the changed default hashes are registered and approved by the maintainer.
note: From ADR 0221 questions 1 and 2, recommendation (b) taken as its own item. Needs the maintainer's lift of the bit-identity rule and approval of the baseline hash changes; not started. Until then a case can set [solver.gradient_equations] pressure = true.

title: Overset meshes in the case tree
acceptance: A case with an overset component runs from a case file; the CLI and the tool surface list it; a registered check reproduces the library result bit for bit.
note: From ADR 0219 question 1, recommendation taken.

title: Overset: several components, a moving background, hole cutting
acceptance: Two component meshes over a background run in one case; a cell cut by a hole is excluded from the solve; the registered conservation check holds.
note: From ADR 0219 questions 2 and 3, recommendation taken.

title: Overset: close the observed-order miss
acceptance: The Taylor-Green order (T1 0.747 against 1.7, T2 level 2 3.31 against 2, T1c 1.618 against 1.7, the F-134 ignored known-miss tests) reaches the registered limits, or the ADR names the donor-interpolation cause with a number.
note: From ADR 0219 question 4, recommendation taken; the known-miss tests stay as recorded.

title: Real-fan parametric study with CMA-ES
acceptance: A CMA-ES study over blade parameters of the 120 mm fan converges within a registered budget and beats the baseline pressure rise at the design flow; the study record is reproducible.
note: From ADR 0222: the real-fan study was split out of F-260. Waits on FAN-01 convergence and the blade-parameter case keys. The design_create_study description change goes with F-310 (golden edit).

title: Wet steam in the case tree
acceptance: A case file with a [wet_steam] table runs the Moses and Stein nozzle and reproduces the library result bit for bit; the key is optional and omitted from the settings hash at its default.
note: From ADR 0217 question 1, recommendation taken. Follows F-317.

title: Wet steam: real-gas vapour model
acceptance: The nozzle's remaining centre-line pressure error (worst -4.93 % at the exit in F-221) is re-measured with a real-gas vapour equation of state against the same 5 % limit, with the margin reported.
note: From ADR 0217 question 2, recommendation taken: F-221 should not be marked done before this.

title: Wet steam: viscous terms
acceptance: The wall boundary layer is solved (no fitted correction) and the exit-pressure deficit of the Moses and Stein nozzle is explained to a registered fraction.
note: From ADR 0217 question 3, recommendation taken: do not fit a boundary-layer correction to the data.

title: Wet steam: polydisperse droplets
acceptance: A method-of-moments droplet spectrum reproduces the measured Sauter radius and the pressure trace of the Moses and Stein nozzle within the F-221 limits.
note: From ADR 0217 question 5, recommendation taken.

title: Wet steam: checks that catch the nucleated-mass term and the wave-speed sound speed
acceptance: New registered checks make mutations MU3 (nucleated-mass term dropped) and MU6 (sound speed in the wave-speed estimates) fail; the F-221 decision rule is applied again and F-221 becomes partial.
note: From ADR 0217 question 9, recommendation taken. MU3 and MU6 survived in F-221. DONE (ADR 0226, 2026-11-08, branch f320-wetsteam-checks, not merged). Test code only (crates/rcfd-fv/tests/wetsteam_f320.rs; no library change, no case key, hashes and goldens untouched). Eight registered fast checks, all met: R1 rates() at the three M1 states against the prototype's decomposition J (4/3) pi r*^3 rho_l + 3 y (dr/dt)/r (worst 2e-8 against 5e-6); L2 a dry box at 285 K, 12 kPa against an ODE written without rates() (y within 1.2e-12 against 1e-6, the liquid is nucleated mass to more than 99.99 percent); A1 the frozen sound speed equals the isentropic derivative of the equation of state (6e-13 against 1e-7); A2 the time step uses it (5e-13); U1 frozen-supersonic face pairs take the upwind flux bit for bit; U2 a supersonic Riemann problem at frozen Mach 1.015 sends nothing upstream (2.2e-16 against 1e-12); negative controls NC3, NC4 (subsonic: 1.8e-5 to 2.2e-4 off the upwind flux, 2.0e-4 upstream). Mutations: MU3 caught by R1 and L2, MU6 by A1, A2, U1, U2 (upstream 8.9e-5); each MU6 site alone (MU6a HLLC, MU6b time step) caught by its own checks; MU1, MU2, MU4, MU5 still caught. The ADR 0217 rule applied again with these checks in its correctness set: every mutation caught, K met, F missed only in part (the coarse run's S1n), V1 met, so F-221 is partial by the rule (recommendation; F-221's entry is the lead's to change). Open: ADR 0226 Q1 (the rule does not write out the case "F missed in part, V1 met"; read as partial), Q2 (the new checks stay in F-221's set).

title: Consistent correctors on the moving-mesh case path
acceptance: A moving-mesh case with [solver.consistent_correctors] enabled runs through the case tree and reproduces the library falling-block result; the edit to ADR 0156 A9b and the Studio scope test are made only with the maintainer's approval.
note: From ADR 0223 question 2. NEEDS THE USER: it edits a registered check (ADR 0156 A9b) and a Studio scope test.

title: Consistent correctors: fold the flags into one key and extend the refused combinations
acceptance: The optional table carries all consistent-corrector flags in one place with a located refusal for each unsupported combination; defaults bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0223 questions 3 and 4, recommendation taken.

title: Droplet models: feedback to the carrier and use with the exchange record
acceptance: Vapour mass, heat and momentum from evaporating and breaking-up parcels are returned to the gas, conserved to 1e-10 relative; the evaporation and breakup models may be used with the particle exchange record.
note: From ADR 0224 question 3, recommendation taken: a separate item before F-252. DONE (ADR 0230, the registration of F-323, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met in the library (rcfd-particles, no case key); the acceptance is still the maintainer's. `Tracker::enable_droplet_exchange()` starts the exchange record of ADR 0057 with the droplet terms, and `advance` then accepts evaporation and breakup (`enable_coupling()` is unchanged and still refuses them). Per sub-step the carrier receives in the start cell the drag with the mass of the start, the heat `m0 c_l (T1 - T0) + dm L_v`, and the vapour `dm` with its momentum `dm v1`, kinetic energy and enthalpy `dm (c_l T1 + L_v)`; gravity, wall and breakup terms are booked so that the balances close; `Coupling::droplet_sources` gives the per-cell mass, momentum and energy sources. Mass, momentum and energy balances at every step: single droplets to 6.9e-16, the spray of ADR 0224 (160 parcels, evaporation and TAB breakup, 300 steps) to 8.8e-16, 2.7e-15 and 1.5e-15 (limit 1e-10); a droplet at its wet bulb draws `L_v` times its mass from the gas to 5.3e-16; the heat of a sub-step is first-order consistent with the model's `Q` (ratio 1.9996); a closed box whose carrier receives the vapour and the heat stops evaporating within 3e-12 K of the adiabatic saturation temperature (limit 1e-6 K). Three negative controls held, seven mutations made their checks fail, no amendment; the record is an observation (fingerprints equal) and the record of ADR 0057 is unchanged bit for bit (the particle suites of rcfd-particles and rcfd-api, H1, baseline hashes). Not in it: no flow solver of rcfd consumes the record; the normal momentum of a TAB breakup is booked as a residual without a carrier counterpart (the source conserves it on the average; 1.45e-3 of the drag impulse in the spray). Open: ADR 0230 Q1 (one method or two), Q2 (breakup momentum), Q3 (enthalpy datum, constant latent heat), Q5 (where the solver wiring goes). Case-tree wiring (optional particles.evaporation and particles.breakup tables, ADR 0224 question 2) goes with F-252. Q5: the recommendation (a separate item) taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11: F-326.

title: Tet mesher: output validity check inside tetrahedralize
acceptance: tetrahedralize checks its output (every cell positive, volume equal to the enclosed volume) and returns a located error instead of an overlapping Ok; the F-306 sweep inputs still give identical meshes.
note: From ADR 0228 question 3, recommendation taken: a small follow-up item. DONE (ADR 0231, the registration of F-324, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met after amendment 2 (a set-up defect of two control tests, corrected before the corrected run); the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0231 Q1). tetrahedralize ends with TetMesh::check_output: every cell positive by the exact orient3d, and the cell volumes equal to the volume enclosed by the output surface within a rigorous rounding bound (Shewchuk's orient3d error bound per simplex, Neumaier summation; about 1e-14 of the volume), else a located Error::Mesh naming the cell, or the first face shared by more than two cells, with two cells on one side, or free but not on the surface. It reads the mesh only: the 111 + 7 fold-free F-306 fingerprints, the R outputs and the existing suites are unchanged; with the F-306 fold put back (MU1) the five overlapping Ok outputs of main become located errors and no overlapping Ok remains. Cost: below 0.1 percent of the mesher's time (F12, F14). Four registered mutations failed their checks. Open: ADR 0231 Q2 (face pairing on every run; the F-247 remesher's outputs), Q3 (the neighbour-link panics). Q2: the recommendation (the remesher follow-up) taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11: F-327.

title: Tet mesher: Linux fingerprint records for the F-306 checks
acceptance: Fingerprints for the 118 fold-free inputs of the F-306 sweep are recorded on Linux by the ADR 0137 procedure at the next Linux gate, and the F-306 N1 checks compare them.
note: From ADR 0228 question 6, recommendation taken. Needs a Linux gate run.

title: Droplet feedback in the transient two-way path
acceptance: With the droplet exchange on, the transient two-way particle path gives the carrier the vapour mass (a species source), the momentum and the energy sources of Coupling::droplet_sources, and the tracker reads the carrier temperature and vapour fraction of the step; gas plus liquid mass, momentum and energy of a closed case are conserved to 1e-10 relative per step; optional particles.evaporation and particles.breakup tables (hash-omitted when absent); a case without them is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0230 question 5, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11 (a separate item, checked by conservation without a data set).

title: F-247 remesher: run the tet output check on its outputs
acceptance: TetRemesher's output meshes pass TetMesh::check_output after every remeshing step, or the step returns its located error; the remesh_f247 hashes stay unchanged.
note: From ADR 0231 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. DONE (ADR 0236, the registration of F-327, 2026-11-12, merged 2026-11-12): every registered check is met at the first run; the acceptance is still the maintainer's (ADR 0236 Q1). TetRemesher::event (and remesh) ends every event that applied an operator with a step check before committing: TetMesh::check_output on the output with the surface of its free faces (the remesher has no stored surface; its boundary is re-triangulated), every free face exactly on its plane, and the cell volume equal to that of the step's input within a rigorous bound (an event does not change the region); a failure returns a located Error::Mesh ("remesh output check: ...", naming the cell, the face or the volumes, and the event's operators and box) and leaves the mesh as it was. The check only reads: M0's hash aaf8f4c36f6446e4 and every P-T number of ADR 0215 are unchanged, and all 1806 P-T events and the 572 events of a geometric piston pass. A duplicated cell, a negative cell, a missing cell and a valid tiling of a changed region are each rejected and located. Cost: 10.3 percent of an event. Four registered mutations failed their checks. Library only; RemeshChange gains the field check. Open: ADR 0236 Q2 (checking new() and motions), Q6 (V2 and V3 not decisive in the piston).

title: Compressible impedance boundary: case-schema wiring
acceptance: `compressible_bc = "impedance"` with `impedance_value` runs the ADR 0233 tube from a case file with R within 1e-2 of the closed form for z/(rho c) = 1/3, 1, 3; located validate errors for a negative impedance and a non-positive pressure; every existing case file's settings hash and written text unchanged after the registered normalisation of the new key at its default.
note: From ADR 0233 question 1, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. NEEDS THE USER before merge: the new key needs an edit of the registered hash test case_hashes_w48u.rs.

title: Sponge layer for the compressible solver
acceptance: A plane pulse leaving through a sponge layer at 0, 30, 45 and 60 degrees reflects less than 1 percent; a case without a sponge is bit-identical.
note: From ADR 0233 question 4, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. Both quiet boundaries reflect 7 percent at 30 degrees and 17 percent at 45 degrees.

title: Frequency-dependent wall impedance (time-domain model)
acceptance: The reflection coefficient of a mass-spring-damper wall matches the closed form in magnitude and phase within 2 percent at three frequencies around the resonance.
note: From ADR 0233, proposed follow-up, taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11.

title: Acoustic wave-equation solver and modal export
acceptance: A duct mode propagates with the closed-form axial wavenumber within 1 percent; a sponge layer ends the duct with less than 1 percent reflection; the modal amplitudes of a synthetic field are exported and recovered within 1 percent.
note: From ADR 0233 question 2, recommendation taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11. The rest of the F-243 title, split from it.

title: SV202's fuller text: what the solvers do with a case without boundary conditions
acceptance: For the compressible solver SV202 states that every patch is a slip wall and an outlet is extrapolated. For every other solver it states that the case is refused unless every mesh patch that is not empty or cyclic has a boundaries entry, and that an entry without keys is a fixed no-slip wall. Each claim is checked through check_only (ADR 0235 A).
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. ADR 0235 A (ADR 0196 Q1 (b), taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): a text change in setup_rules.json, a registered edit of rules_w19c.rs E5 and a new check E6; all checks met, two mutations caught. No golden held the text.

title: `rcfd map --warm-start extended`: the extended warm start on the command line
acceptance: With --warm-start extended, a map of an energy or two-equation-turbulence case restarts each point warm, and its reports agree with cold runs within REL_WARM 1e-4. Without the flag, or with flow, the map tables are byte-identical to before (ADR 0235 B).
note: DONE pending acceptance, merged 2026-11-12. ADR 0235 B (ADR 0209 Q7 (c), taken on the maintainer's standing instruction of 2026-11-11): HE map warm against cold 5.7e-9, 61 and 60 iterations against 89 and 88; defaults byte-identical; three mutations caught. Open: the extended start as the map default (Q7 (b)) and in the design tools (Q7 (a), a golden edit).
